{"final_story":"## Misi PSLV-C56: Penjelajah Antariksa dari India untuk Singapura

Malam itu, di laboratorium fisika sekolah, Maya, seorang siswi kelas sebelas yang dikenal cerdas dan selalu haus akan pengetahuan, tampak serius menatap layar komputernya. Di sampingnya, Bima, sahabatnya yang juga memiliki ketertarikan pada antariksa, sibuk mengutak-atik model roket kecil buatannya.

“Maya, coba lihat ini!” seru Bima tiba-tiba, “Aku barusan baca berita tentang peluncuran roket PSLV-C56. Kedengarannya seru banget, misi komersial dari India untuk Singapura!”

Maya mengalihkan pandangannya dari layar. “Oh ya? PSLV-C56? Aku pernah dengar sekilas. Roket kebanggaan India, kan? Tapi kapan tepatnya peluncurannya, dan dari mana?”

Bima menggaruk kepalanya. “Nah, itu dia! Beritanya cukup detail, tapi kadang aku bingung memilah informasi pentingnya. Coba kita bedah bersama, yuk?”

Maya tersenyum. “Ide bagus! Ini bisa jadi proyek mini kita untuk memahami misi-misi antariksa. Oke, siap!”

Mereka mulai membaca informasi yang ditemukan Bima dengan seksama.

**Bima:** “Oke, pertama, informasi dasar tentang misi ini. Katanya, PSLV-C56 ini adalah misi ke-58 dari **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** milik **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. Itu lembaga antariksa India, kan?”

**Maya:** “Betul sekali! ISRO ini agensi antariksa yang didirikan tahun 1969, pelopor banyak kemajuan di bidang antariksa India, termasuk peluncuran satelit pertamanya, Aryabhata, di tahun 1975. Jadi, PSLV-C56 ini menunjukkan konsistensi ISRO dalam berkarya. Dan bukan cuma itu, ini juga merupakan penerbangan ke-17 dari varian **PSLV-CA**. Berarti ada beberapa varian roket PSLV yang berbeda, ya?”

**Bima:** “Sepertinya begitu! Jadi, ini bukan roket PSLV yang sembarangan, tapi varian yang sudah terbukti. Nah, sekarang ke inti pertanyaanku, Maya: **Kapan jadwal peluncurannya?**”

Maya menunjuk ke paragraf spesifik di layar. “Ini dia! Peluncurannya dijadwalkan pada **Minggu, 30 Juli 2023**. Dan kita harus ingat, ada dua zona waktu yang disebutkan di sini: **pukul 06:30 IST / 01:00 UTC**.”

**Bima:** “IST itu waktu India, ya? Kalau UTC itu waktu universal. Jadi, supaya nggak bingung, kalau kita mau nonton live streaming, kita harus konversi ke waktu Indonesia. Pukul 06:30 IST… itu sekitar jam 08:00 WIB kalau di Indonesia bagian Barat. Wah, lumayan pagi!”

**Maya:** “Tepat! Penting untuk memperhatikan perbedaan zona waktu agar tidak ketinggalan momen penting. Lalu, pertanyaan kedua, **Dari mana roket ini akan diluncurkan?**”

Bima mencari-cari lagi. “Ketemu! Disebutkan akan diluncurkan dari **Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, India**. Dan lebih spesifik lagi, dari **First Launch Pad (FLP)**.”

**Maya:** “Sip! Jadi, Satish Dhawan Space Centre di Sriharikota itu adalah fasilitas utama peluncuran antariksa milik ISRO. Ibaratnya seperti Cape Canaveral-nya Amerika Serikat. Dan First Launch Pad menunjukkan bahwa ada banyak landasan peluncuran di sana. Ini menunjukkan betapa canggihnya infrastruktur antariksa India.”

**Bima:** “Menarik sekali! Jadi, intinya begini: **PSLV-C56 akan diluncurkan pada Minggu, 30 Juli 2023, pukul 06:30 IST / 01:00 UTC, dari Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, India, tepatnya dari First Launch Pad (FLP)**.”

**Maya:** “Sempurna! Dan sebagai informasi tambahan yang penting, misi ini adalah misi komersial yang didedikasikan melalui NSIL, membawa **DS-SAR sebagai satelit utama** dan **VELOX-AM sebagai satelit sekunder, ditambah 5 satelit lainnya**. Dan yang paling menarik, **semua satelit yang dibawa dalam misi ini adalah milik Singapura**.”

**Bima:** “Wow! Jadi, India meluncurkan satelit untuk negara lain. Ini menunjukkan betapa majunya program antariksa mereka dan juga bagaimana kerja sama internasional di bidang ini semakin berkembang. Keren banget!”

Maya mengangguk. “Betul sekali, Bima. Misi PSLV-C56 ini bukan hanya sekadar peluncuran roket, tetapi juga cerminan kemajuan teknologi, pentingnya kerja sama global, dan bagaimana sains serta rekayasa dapat menghubungkan berbagai negara. Siapa tahu, suatu hari nanti kita berdua bisa terlibat dalam misi seperti ini!”

Bima tersenyum lebar. “Amin! Sekarang sudah jelas seperti kristal. Terima kasih, Maya! Kita sudah berhasil membedah informasi penting dari berita ini. Siap-siap pasang alarm untuk nonton peluncuran PSLV-C56!”

Mereka berdua kembali menatap layar, kali ini dengan pemahaman yang lebih mendalam dan semangat yang membara untuk lebih banyak lagi mempelajari keajaiban antariksa. At 120 metres (394 feet) in height and with a liftoff mass of 5,000 metric tons (11,000,000 pounds), Starship is the largest and most powerful rocket ever flown, surpassing the thrust of NASA's Space Launch System and Saturn V, as well as the Soviet N1, which had previously held the record.The two-stage-to-orbit launch vehicle consists of the first-stage Super Heavy booster and the second-stage spacecraft also named Starship. Both stages are powered by Raptor rocket engines, which burn liquid methane and liquid oxygen, operating in a full-flow staged combustion power cycle. Both are designed to be fully reusable, performing controlled landings on the arms of the launch tower used to lift the vehicles and, eventually, reflown within hours. Starship is designed to have a payload capacity of 150 tonnes (330,000 lb) to low Earth orbit in a fully reusable configuration and 250 t (550,000 lb) when expended. Starship vehicles in low Earth orbit are planned to be refilled with propellant launched in tanker Starships to enable transit to higher energy destinations such as geosynchronous orbit, the Moon, and Mars.Plans for a heavy-lift vehicle at SpaceX date to 2005, with the earliest concept resembling the modern vehicle announced in 2016. SpaceX's Starship development follows an iterative and incremental approach involving frequent, and often destructive, test flights of prototype vehicles. The first and so far only orbital test flight was attempted on 20 April 2023, when an anomaly caused the vehicle to tumble out of control four minutes after launch. SpaceX activated the flight termination system, which fired the explosive charges but did not destroy the vehicle. Approximately 40 seconds later both stages were destroyed due to increased aerodynamic forces.  After the test, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grounded the launch program pending results of a standard "mishap investigation".SpaceX intends Starship to become its primary launch vehicle, superseding the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launch vehicles as well as the Dragon 2 spacecraft currently used as part of NASA's commercial crew program to the International Space Station. Starship is often coupled with the company's Mars ambitions. Planned Starship flights include the development of SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, crewed flights under the Polaris and dearMoon programs, and two crewed lunar landings with a modified Starship spacecraft under the Artemis program.

History
Starting with a 2012 announcement of plans to develop a rocket with substantially greater capabilities than SpaceX's existing Falcon 9—underpinned by the ambition to enable human exploration and settlement of Mars—the company created a succession of preliminary designs for such a vehicle, under various names (Mars Colonial Transporter, Interplanetary Transport System, BFR) leading up to a 2019 adoption of a stainless-steel body design, which is also when the name changed to the current Starship. SpaceX has since been applying the iterative design methodology, using intensive tests on a series of rocket prototypes. The first prototype, Starhopper, performed several static fires and low-altitude flights. Seven of Starship's upper-stage prototypes were flight tested between August 2020 and May 2021. The last of the seven, a full-size Starship SN15, successfully landed after reaching an altitude of 10 kilometers (6.2 mi). A full-scale orbital test flight of the rocket took place on April 20, 2023.

In 2007, Elon Musk publicly stated that he hopes to enable the exploration and settlement of Mars through SpaceX. SpaceX began developing the Raptor rocket engine before 2014. From 2011 to 2014, Musk made various statements expressing his hope that SpaceX would send humans to Mars in the 2020s to 2030s.

Mars Colonial Transporter
In October 2012, Musk made the first public articulation of plans to develop a fully reusable rocket system with substantially greater capabilities than SpaceX's existing Falcon 9. This new launch vehicle was intended to be part of the company's Mars system architecture, then known as the Mars Colonial Transporter/Mass Cargo Transport (MCT). According to SpaceX, the MCT system would include reusable rocket engines, launch vehicles and space capsules that would enable transportation of humans to Mars and back to Earth. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell gave a potential payload range between 150-200 tonnes to low Earth orbit for the planned rocket. According to SpaceX, the MCT was to be "going to be much bigger [than Falcon 9]". In February 2014, the planned principal payload for the MCT was announced to be a large interplanetary spacecraft, designed to carry up to 100 tonnes (220,000 lb) of passengers and cargo. According to SpaceX engine development head Tom Mueller, SpaceX could use nine Raptor engines on a single spacecraft. The preliminary rocket design was to be at least 10 meters (33 ft) in diameter and was expected to have up to three cores totaling at least 27 booster engines.

In 2016, Musk changed the name of the Mars Colonial Transporter system to the Interplanetary Transport System  (ITS), as he intended for the system to be capable of traveling beyond Mars. That same year he provided more details about the space mission architecture, launch vehicle, spacecraft, and Raptor engines. The center cluster of seven engines was to be gimbaled for directional control, although some directional control  was to be performed via differential thrust on the fixed engines.

{"final_story": "Tentu, ini adalah cerita edukatif tentang Jejak Zubaydah:

## Petualangan di Jejak Zubaydah: Sebuah Kisah Abad Pertengahan

Matahari gurun membakar tanpa ampun, memantulkan sinarnya di pasir keemasan yang terbentang sejauh mata memandang. Di tengah panas terik itu, sesosok karavan bergerak perlahan, unta-unta melenguh lelah, langkah para peziarah terasa berat. Di antara mereka, seorang gadis muda bernama Aisha menghela napas. "Ayah," tanyanya, suaranya sedikit serak, "kapan kita akan mencapai perhentian berikutnya? Aku sangat haus."

Ayahnya, seorang pedagang bijak dari Kufah, tersenyum tipis. "Sabar, Aisha. Kita sedang mengikuti Jejak Zubaydah. Tidak lama lagi kita akan menemukan sumur atau kolam. Ini adalah jalan yang telah dibangun dengan susah payah untuk kenyamanan seperti kita."

Aisha mengerutkan kening. "Jejak Zubaydah? Siapa itu Zubaydah, Ayah? Dan kapan jalan ini dibangun?"

Ayahnya mengangguk, melirik ke arah tanda batu yang samar di kejauhan. "Ah, itu adalah cerita yang patut didengar, putriku. Jejak Zubaydah, atau kadang disebut juga rute ziarah Al-Kufi, adalah salah satu dari tujuh rute ziarah utama di Semenanjung Arab. Bayangkan, rute ini sudah ada lebih dari 1000 tahun! Jauh sebelum kita lahir, bahkan sebelum kakek buyutmu."

"Seribu tahun?" mata Aisha membulat. "Itu sangat tua!"

"Betul sekali," lanjut Ayahnya. "Sebenarnya, jalan ini sudah digunakan oleh suku-suku, pedagang, dan kafilah jauh sebelum Islam datang. Mereka menggunakannya untuk bergerak antara Irak dan Arab Barat. Tapi, seiring waktu, tempat-tempat penting seperti sumber air, padang rumput, dan lokasi pertambangan di sepanjang jalan ini mulai berubah menjadi stasiun-stasiun besar."

"Jadi, kapan Jejak Zubaydah ini benar-benar 'dibangun' seperti yang kita lihat sekarang, dengan semua fasilitasnya?" tanya Aisha, kini lebih tertarik.

"Itu terjadi pada masa Kekhalifahan Abbasiyah," jelas Ayahnya. "Periode Abbasiyah itu berlangsung antara tahun 132 Hijriah (sekitar 750 Masehi) hingga 656 Hijriah (sekitar 1258 Masehi). Pada masa itulah, para Khalifah Abbasiyah, terutama yang sangat peduli pada kesejahteraan para peziarah, mulai mengembangkan dan memperluas jalan ini secara besar-besaran."

"Dan siapa Zubaydah itu?" desak Aisha.

Ayahnya tersenyum hangat. "Zubaydah adalah nama seorang wanita yang luar biasa, putri Khalifah Abu Ja'far al-Mansur dan istri dari Khalifah Harun al-Rashid yang terkenal. Kisahnya bermula ketika ia sendiri melakukan perjalanan haji pada tahun 176 Hijriah. Ia mengalami kesulitan yang luar biasa dalam perjalanannya – panas, haus, dan kurangnya tempat istirahat."

"Oh, sama seperti kita sekarang!" seru Aisha.

"Persis," kata Ayahnya. "Dan karena pengalamannya itu, Ratu Zubaydah tergerak hatinya. Ia memerintahkan pembangunan tempat peristirahatan dan kolam-kolam air di sepanjang rute ini. Bayangkan, ia merancang sistem yang rapi untuk mengumpulkan air hujan, aliran sungai, dan limpasan air ke dalam kanal-kanal air. Ia dan suaminya bahkan mengorbankan sebagian besar kekayaan mereka untuk kenyamanan para peziarah dan musafir."

"Jadi, jalan ini dinamai untuk menghormatinya?"

"Benar sekali. Berkat sumbangsihnya yang besar, jalan ini dikenal sebagai Jejak Zubaydah. Itu adalah bukti nyata betapa pedulinya ia terhadap orang lain."

target_age: "15-18"

Context:
The Zubaydah Trail (Al-Kufi pilgrimage route) is among the seven major pilgrimage routes in the Arabian Peninsula, dating back over 1000 years. A crucial trade route during the Abbasid era, it is a strong candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage List. This historical trail was constructed to serve pilgrims from Iraq, neighbouring Islamic countries, and East Asian countries.
Its construction was completed during the Abbasid Caliphate, specifically between 132 AH (750 CE) and 656 AH (1258 CE). 
The trail's history dates back to the pre-Islamic era, when it was used by tribes, travellers, and commercial caravans to move between Iraq and Western Arabia. Over time, its usage became regular and easier as the water centres, grazing areas, and mining locations along the route transformed into major stations.
During the Abbasid era, the trail served as an important link between Baghdad, the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, and the rest of the Arabian Peninsula. The Abbasid caliphs took great interest in the trail, enhanced it with various benefits and facilities, as well as undertook an expansion of the road to make it suitable for use by pilgrims, travellers, and their animals.Historical, geographical, and archaeological sources show that the trail route was designed in a practical and meticulous manner. Along its length from Kufa to Mecca, stations, houses, and resting areas were established. Its surface was paved with stones in sandy and muddy areas. In addition, it was equipped with necessary amenities and facilities such as wells, ponds, and dams. Signages, lighthouses, beacons, and stoves were also set up to mark its path and guide travellers.The Zubaydah Trail stretches over a distance of 1,300 kilometres and is connected to 27 main stations, most of which are concentrated in Saudi Arabia. Furthermore, 58 subsidiary stations called Muta'asha, which are rest stops, were established between every two main stations. The average distance between each main station and the next is approximately 50 kilometres.

{"final_story": "Tentu, ini adalah cerita edukatif tentang krisis ekonomi Sri Lanka yang ditujukan untuk siswa berusia 15-18 tahun.

---

**Judul: Badai di Pulau Permata: Kisah Krisis Ekonomi Sri Lanka**

Dahulu kala, di sebuah pulau yang indah dan subur bernama Sri Lanka, hidup seorang gadis muda bernama Anya. Anya berusia 16 tahun, cerdas, dan selalu ingin tahu. Ia sering mendengar orang dewasa membicarakan "krisis ekonomi" dan "kesulitan hidup" di negaranya. Anya ingin sekali memahami apa yang sebenarnya terjadi.

Suatu sore, Anya bertanya kepada pamannya, Pak Wijaya, seorang pensiunan guru ekonomi. "Paman, mengapa harga-harga menjadi sangat mahal? Mengapa kita sulit mendapatkan bensin dan obat-obatan? Apa yang sebenarnya terjadi pada ekonomi Sri Lanka?"

Pak Wijaya tersenyum lembut. "Pertanyaan bagus, Anya. Krisis ini seperti badai besar yang menghantam sebuah kapal. Banyak faktor yang menyebabkan badai itu datang. Mari paman ceritakan perlahan."

**Faktor Pertama: Kebijakan Pajak yang Terburu-buru (Penguras Lautan)**

"Bayangkan sebuah negara seperti sebuah rumah tangga besar," mulai Pak Wijaya. "Pemerintah adalah kepala rumah tangga yang mengumpulkan uang dari pajak warga, seperti gaji. Uang itu digunakan untuk membeli makanan, membayar listrik, membangun jalan, dan lain-lain."

"Pada tahun 2019, pemerintah kita memutuskan untuk memotong banyak pajak. Mereka pikir ini akan mendorong orang untuk berbelanja dan berinvestasi lebih banyak," jelas Pak Wijaya. "Tapi, ibaratnya, mereka terlalu banyak menguras air dari sumur kita. Pendapatan pemerintah langsung anjlok drastis. Akibatnya, uang untuk membiayai kebutuhan negara menjadi sangat kurang."

Anya mengerutkan kening. "Jadi, seperti kalau ayahku gajinya dipotong, kita akan kesulitan membayar kebutuhan rumah tangga?"

"Tepat sekali, Anya! Karena pendapatan negara berkurang, lembaga pemeringkat internasional menurunkan peringkat kredit kita. Ini seperti bank yang menilai seseorang tidak mampu membayar utang, sehingga sulit bagi negara kita untuk meminjam uang lagi dari luar negeri."

**Faktor Kedua: Mencetak Uang Terlalu Banyak (Menggandakan Kertas, Bukan Kekayaan)**

"Karena uang pajak berkurang, pemerintah mencari cara lain untuk membiayai pengeluaran," lanjut Pak Wijaya. "Mereka mulai mencetak uang dalam jumlah besar. Ini seperti kalau kamu kekurangan uang jajan, lalu kamu menggambar uang sendiri di kertas. Apakah uang gambaran itu bisa membeli permen?"

Anya tertawa. "Tentu saja tidak, Paman!"

"Benar. Mencetak uang terlalu banyak tanpa didukung oleh produksi barang dan jasa yang nyata, justru membuat nilai uang kita jatuh. Ini namanya **inflasi**. Barang-barang menjadi sangat mahal karena uang yang beredar terlalu banyak, tapi barangnya tetap sama. Akibatnya, daya beli masyarakat menurun drastis. Ini yang membuat harga bensin, makanan, dan obat-obatan melambung tinggi."

**Faktor Ketiga: Pergeseran Pertanian Organik Mendadak (Menjatuhkan Sekop di Tengah Jalan)**

"Pernahkah kamu mendengar tentang kebijakan pertanian organik?" tanya Pak Wijaya. "Pemerintah kita saat itu memutuskan untuk melarang penggunaan pupuk kimia dan pestisida secara tiba-tiba, dengan harapan menjadi negara pertama di dunia yang sepenuhnya organik."

"Kedengarannya bagus, Paman. Lebih sehat, kan?" kata Anya.

"Memang tujuannya baik, Anya. Tapi pelaksanaannya terlalu mendadak dan tanpa persiapan yang matang. Petani kita belum siap dengan metode organik skala besar. Akibatnya, hasil panen, terutama beras dan teh (ekspor utama kita), anjlok drastis. Kita bahkan harus mengimpor beras, padahal dulu kita mandiri pangan."

"Ini seperti kamu sedang membangun rumah, lalu tiba-tiba semua tukang disuruh berhenti memakai alat modern dan hanya boleh memakai alat tradisional. Pekerjaan pasti jadi lambat dan hasilnya kurang maksimal," jelas Pak Wijaya. "Penurunan hasil pertanian ini berdampak besar pada ketersediaan pangan dan juga pemasukan devisa dari ekspor."

**Faktor Keempat: Serangan Teroris dan Pandemi (Badai Tak Terduga)**

"Selain masalah internal, ada juga badai dari luar," kata Pak Wijaya dengan nada prihatin. "Pada tahun 2019, terjadi serangan bom Paskah yang mengerikan. Ini sangat merusak industri pariwisata kita, yang merupakan salah satu sumber utama devisa negara."

"Lalu, pandemi COVID-19 datang. Pembatasan perjalanan dan penutupan perbatasan membuat pariwisata lumpuh total. Pekerja migran kita yang mengirimkan uang dari luar negeri juga banyak yang kehilangan pekerjaan. Akibatnya, pemasukan devisa negara semakin menipis."

Anya menghela napas. "Jadi, devisa itu seperti tabungan negara dalam mata uang asing, Paman?"

"Tepat sekali! Devisa sangat penting untuk membayar impor barang-barang penting seperti bahan bakar, obat-obatan, dan bahan baku industri. Ketika devisa menipis, kita tidak bisa membeli barang-barang ini dari luar negeri, sehingga terjadi kelangkaan dan harga semakin naik."

**Faktor Kelima: Utang Luar Negeri yang Menumpuk (Beban yang Terlalu Berat)**

"Sejak lama, Sri Lanka memiliki kebiasaan meminjam uang dari negara lain dan lembaga internasional," jelas Pak Wijaya. "Dulu, kebanyakan pinjaman untuk proyek pembangunan yang penting. Namun, belakangan ini, banyak pinjaman yang digunakan untuk proyek-proyek 'megah' yang tidak menghasilkan keuntungan ekonomi yang signifikan."

"Utang ini terus menumpuk. Ketika devisa menipis, kita kesulitan membayar cicilan utang. Ini seperti kamu punya banyak utang kartu kredit, tapi gajimu dipotong dan kamu tidak bisa membayar cicilan. Akhirnya, kamu dinyatakan bangkrut."

"Pada tahun 2022, Sri Lanka resmi menyatakan gagal bayar utang. Ini berarti kita tidak mampu membayar utang-utang kita, yang merupakan hal yang sangat serius dan baru pertama kali terjadi sejak kemerdekaan kita."

**Kesimpulan: Pelajaran dari Badai**

"Jadi, Anya," Pak Wijaya mengakhiri penjelasannya, "krisis ekonomi Sri Lanka adalah hasil dari kombinasi beberapa faktor: kebijakan pajak yang salah, pencetakan uang yang berlebihan, perubahan kebijakan pertanian yang terburu-buru, serangan teroris, pandemi, dan beban utang luar negeri yang menumpuk."

"Ini adalah pelajaran berharga bahwa sebuah negara harus memiliki manajemen ekonomi yang hati-hati, perencanaan yang matang, dan tidak boleh mengambil keputusan penting secara terburu-buru tanpa mempertimbangkan dampaknya secara menyeluruh. Kita harus belajar dari kesalahan ini agar badai seperti ini tidak terulang lagi."

Anya mengangguk pelan, wajahnya menunjukkan pemahaman yang lebih dalam. "Terima kasih, Paman. Sekarang aku mengerti mengapa Sri Lanka kita mengalami kesulitan ini. Ini bukan hanya satu masalah, tapi banyak masalah yang terjadi bersamaan."

"Benar, Anya. Dan penting bagi kalian para generasi muda untuk memahami ini, agar kelak kalian bisa menjadi warga negara yang kritis dan berkontribusi dalam membangun masa depan yang lebih baik untuk Sri Lanka."

Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What factors contributed to the Sri Lankan economic crisis?

target_age: "15-18"
story_style: "educational"

Context:
The Sri Lankan economic crisis is an ongoing crisis in the island country of Sri Lanka that started in 2019. It is the country's worst economic crisis since its independence in 1948. It has led to unprecedented levels of inflation, near-depletion of foreign exchange reserves, shortages of medical supplies, and an increase in prices of basic commodities. The crisis is said to have begun due to multiple compounding factors like tax cuts, money creation, a nationwide policy to shift to organic or biological farming, the 2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka. The subsequent economic hardships resulted in the 2022 Sri Lankan protests.
Sri Lanka had been earmarked for sovereign default, as the remaining foreign exchange reserves of US$1.9 billion as of March 2022 would not be sufficient to pay the country's foreign debt obligations for 2022, with $4 billion to be repaid. An International Sovereign Bond repayment of $1 billion was due to be paid by the government in July 2022. Bloomberg reported that Sri Lanka had a total of $8.6 billion in repayments due in 2022, including both local debt and foreign debt. In April 2022, the Sri Lankan government announced that it was defaulting, making it the first sovereign default in Sri Lankan history since its independence in 1948 and the first state in the Asia-Pacific region to enter sovereign default in the 21st century.In June 2022, then Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said in parliament that the economy had collapsed, leaving it unable to pay for essentials.In September 2022, a United Nations report said that the economic crisis is a result of officials' impunity for human rights abuses and economic crimes. According to the Sri Lankan finance ministry, the country's foreign reserves had grown by 23.5% from US$1.7 billion in September 2022 to US$2.1 billion in February 2023, representing a US$400 million increase. Sri Lanka teeters on the edge of financial insolvency and has halted repayments on its international debts.

Background
According to W. A. Wijewardena, a former Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the country was a long way into an economic crisis in 2015. The government that came into power in 2015 knew this and had been warned by the Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka about a number of risks. While the then Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe in 2015 had presented a strong economic policy to address the situation, the coalition government could not get the policy pushed through Parliament, which would eventually result in further policy confusion in the coming months.The government did not adequately address the economic warnings and emerging dangers, consuming itself in other government related activities such as "constitutional reforms". Certain practices, including those used by the Ministry of Finance led by Ravi Karunanayake, were globally frowned upon. Election related economic decisions were pushed such as excessive distribution of freebies. The Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka's 2014 State of the Economy Report highlighted hot money, worrying borrowing practices, temporary and superficial quick-fixes and monopoly of foreign direct investment flow into the hospitality sector.Further political turmoil in 2018 worsened the economic outlook. By that time the government had carried out several reforms under an IMF supported program towards fiscal monetary consolidation and had successfully controlled inflation. These reforms included an automatic fuel pricing formula which significantly reduced fiscal risks posed by state-owned enterprises (SOEs), raised the value-added tax (VAT) rate from 11 percent to 15 percent, and broadened the VAT base by removing exemptions. Many of the reforms were reversed by the new government after the 2019 elections.Under Maithripala Sirisena administration, the 2019 Central Bank Bill was drafted to make the Central Bank independent from political influence by banning the Treasury Secretary and any member of the Government from becoming members of the Monetary Board. Money printing was also to be banned under this bill, as it states: "The Central Bank shall not purchase securities issued by the government, by any government-owned entity, or any other public entity in the primary market." Then Central Bank Governor, Indrajit Coomaraswamy, noted Balance of Payments issues, increased inflation, and asset bubbles as reasons for the ban. The Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna Party opposed an independent Central Bank and discarded the bill as soon as they came to power.Many experts compared Lebanon's economic situation with that of Sri Lanka and had warned that Sri Lanka too was on the way to defaulting on its sovereign bonds. Both nations had similar issues, including deep economic crises occurring after their successive governments piled up unsustainable debts following the end of civil wars. To reduce the inflation and control the economy crisis in April 2022, Dr. P. Nandalal Weerasinghe was appointed as the 17th Governor of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) to replace Ajith Nivard Cabraal.

Causes
Tax cuts and money creation
The Government of Sri Lanka under president Gotabaya Rajapaksa made large tax cuts that affected government revenue and fiscal policies, causing budget deficits to soar.  These cuts included increased tax-free thresholds that resulted in a 33.5% decline in registered taxpayers, reducing VAT to 8%, reducing corporate tax from  28% to 24%, the abolishment of the Pay As You Earn (PAYE) tax and the 2% “nation-building tax” which financed infrastructure development. The massive loss of tax revenue resulted in rating agencies downgrading the sovereign credit rating making it harder to take more debt. In 2021 P. B. Jayasundera stated that President Rajapaksa was aware of the loss of revenue but considered it an "investment" and had no plans of increasing taxes for another 5 years.To cover government spending, the Central Bank began printing money in record amounts ignoring advice from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to stop printing money and instead hike interest rates and raise taxes while cutting spending.  The IMF warned that continuing to print money would lead to an economic implosion. The tax cuts were also opposed by the former Finance Minister Mangala Samaraweera who noted that as the Sri Lankan government already had far less tax revenue relative to most countries which combined with its high debt load tax cuts would be dangerous. Samaraweera predicted that “If these proposals are implemented like this not only will the entire country go bankrupt, but the entire country will become another Venezuela or another Greece.”On 6 April 2022, the CBSL allegedly printed 119.08 billion rupees, making it the highest reported amount printed on a single day by the CBSL for the year 2022. The total money added to financial markets for the year 2022 increased to Rs. 432.76 billion.

External debt
Until mid-2000s, the Sri Lankan debt was mainly from multilateral lending agencies, after which it was reoriented under the leadership of Mahinda Rajapaksa to foreign investors and lenders. Sri Lanka issues its first international sovereign bond in 2007, with high interest rates to incentivise investors. According to commentators, the money was used to fund vanity projects rather than projects of national utility.Sri Lanka's foreign debt increased substantially, going from US$11.3 billion in 2005 to $56.3 billion in 2020. While foreign debt was about 42% of the GDP in 2019, it rose to 119% of its GDP in 2021. By February 2022, the country had only $2.31 billion left in its reserves, yet faces debt repayments of around $4 billion in 2022, which also includes a $1 billion international sovereign bond (ISB) maturing in July.In 2020, US economist Joseph Eugene Stiglitz, published a report that blamed the quantitative easing policy made by US banks after 2008, for exporting debt bubbles to deve

. This has raised concerns about the country's ability to meet its financial obligations and maintain its economic stability.

The declining reserves can be attributed to several factors. Firstly, the COVID-19 pandemic has severely impacted the country's economy, leading to a decrease in export revenues and foreign direct investment. This has resulted in a decline in foreign currency inflows, putting pressure on the country's reserves.

Secondly, the country has been facing a persistent current account deficit, meaning that it is importing more goods and services than it is exporting. This has further strained the country's reserves as it needs to use foreign currency to pay for these imports.

Additionally, the country has been grappling with high levels of external debt. The debt repayments, including the maturing ISB, add to the financial burden and put further strain on the country's reserves.

To address these challenges, the country may need to take several measures. Firstly, it could seek financial assistance from international organizations such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) or the World Bank. This could provide the country with the necessary funds to meet its debt obligations and stabilize its reserves.

Secondly, the country could implement policies to boost its export revenues and reduce its reliance on imports. This could include promoting domestic industries, diversifying its export markets, and improving the business environment to attract foreign investment.

Furthermore, the country could explore options to restructure its debt, such as negotiating with creditors to extend repayment periods or reduce interest rates. This could help alleviate the immediate financial pressure and provide the country with more breathing room to manage its reserves.

Overall, the declining reserves and upcoming debt repayments pose significant challenges for the country's economic stability. However, with the right measures and support from international organizations, the country can work towards addressing these challenges and ensuring its long-term financial sustainability.

**Proyek “Bayangan Langit”**

Desas-desus berawal di kelas Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam Pak Ardi. Hari itu, topik diskusi adalah tentang alat-alat pengumpul data cuaca.

"Siapa yang bisa memberi tahu saya, alat apa yang biasa digunakan untuk memprediksi cuaca?" tanya Pak Ardi, sambil tersenyum ke arah seisi kelas.

Bella, siswa yang selalu bersemangat, mengangkat tangannya. "Balon cuaca, Pak! Biasanya kecil dan dilepaskan ke atmosfer untuk mengukur suhu, tekanan, dan kelembaban."

"Tepat sekali, Bella!" Pak Ardi mengangguk. "Tapi, bagaimana jika ada sebuah balon yang ukurannya jauh lebih besar dari balon cuaca biasa, dan justru terbang di atas beberapa negara tanpa izin?"

Sontak, seluruh kelas hening. Pak Ardi kemudian memutar sebuah video pendek. Video itu menunjukkan sebuah benda putih besar melayang di langit biru.

"Ini adalah 'Balon Misteri' yang menjadi berita utama awal tahun ini," Pak Ardi memulai ceritanya. "Balon ini milik Tiongkok, dan terlihat di wilayah udara Amerika Utara dari akhir Januari hingga awal Februari 2023."

Rizal, siswa yang selalu penasaran dengan teknologi, bertanya, "Tapi, Pak, kenapa balon Tiongkok bisa terbang di sana? Bukankah itu berarti melanggar kedaulatan negara lain?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Rizal," jawab Pak Ardi. "Pemerintah Tiongkok mengklaim itu adalah balon sipil, kebanyakan untuk tujuan meteorologi, yang kebetulan terbawa angin. Namun, Amerika Serikat memiliki pandangan yang berbeda."

Pak Ardi berjalan ke papan tulis dan mulai menggambar. "Bayangkan ini adalah balon raksasa itu." Dia menggambar sebuah lingkaran besar. "Para pejabat AS mengatakan bahwa ukuran balon ini sangatlah masif. Tingginya sekitar 61 meter. Itu kira-kira setinggi gedung 20 lantai!"

Mata para siswa terbelalak. "Wow!" seru beberapa dari mereka.

"Diameter balonnya sendiri sekitar 45 meter," lanjut Pak Ardi. "Bahkan para ahli mengatakan balon cuaca biasa ukurannya kurang dari seperempat dari diameter balon ini. Jadi, ini jelas bukan balon cuaca biasa."

Sekar, yang terkenal kritis, bertanya, "Kalau bukan balon cuaca biasa, lalu apa isinya, Pak?"

Pak Ardi tersenyum teka-teki. "Nah, itu dia bagian yang paling menarik. Bagian penting dari balon ini adalah 'muatannya' atau yang sering disebut sebagai 'payload'. "Bayangkan ukuran payload ini," kata Pak Ardi. "Menurut perkiraan awal, ukurannya sebesar dua hingga tiga bus sekolah!"

"Dua bus sekolah?!" seru Bima, terkejut. "Besar sekali!"

"Benar sekali, Bima. Dan bobotnya? Diperkirakan lebih dari 910 kilogram!" Pak Ardi menambahkan. "Bahkan Presiden AS Joe Biden menggambarkannya sebagai membawa peralatan mata-mata seberat dua gerbong kereta api!"

Siswa-siswa saling berbisik, kagum dengan informasi tersebut.

"Apa yang ada di dalam payload sebesar itu, Pak?" tanya Bella lagi.

"Setelah balon itu ditembak jatuh dan serpihannya dikumpulkan, para ahli menganalisisnya di laboratorium FBI. Mereka menemukan bahwa payload itu dilengkapi dengan antena dan peralatan lain yang kemungkinan digunakan untuk mengumpulkan sinyal komunikasi. Sinyal intelijen, lho," jelas Pak Ardi. "Ada juga panel surya yang terpasang pada payload, jumlahnya sampai enam belas buah, untuk memberikan daya pada seluruh peralatan canggih itu."

Rian, yang selalu memperhatikan detail teknis, bertanya, "Kalau begitu, bagaimana balon sebesar itu bergerak, Pak? Apa terbawa angin saja?"

"Lagi-lagi pertanyaan yang bagus, Rian!" Pak Ardi menunjuk ke gambar di papan tulis. "Meskipun Tiongkok mengklaimnya terbawa angin, pejabat AS mengatakan balon itu memiliki baling-baling dan kemudi. Jadi, balon ini sebenarnya bisa bermanuver, meskipun kemampuan kendalinya terbatas."

Pak Ardi kemudian menjelaskan lebih jauh. "Balon ini jenis 'superpressure balloon'. Artinya, volumenya relatif konstan walaupun ada perubahan tekanan atau suhu di luar. "Tapi Pak, kalau memang sebesar itu dan bisa mengumpulkan informasi, kenapa pemerintah AS membiarkannya terbang dulu?" tanya Sekar.

"Itu juga pertanyaan yang sempat muncul ke publik," jawab Pak Ardi. "Pentagon mengatakan balon itu tidak menimbulkan ancaman militer atau fisik bagi orang-orang di darat. Akhirnya, pada tanggal 4 Februari 2023, Angkatan Udara AS menembak jatuh balon tersebut di atas perairan teritorial AS di lepas pantai Carolina Selatan. Puing-puingnya kemudian dikumpulkan untuk analisis lebih lanjut.

"Insiden ini memperlihatkan betapa canggihnya teknologi pengawasan udara yang ada saat ini," tutup Pak Ardi. story_style: "educational"
language: "Indonesian"

Context:
From January 28 to February 4, 2023, a high-altitude balloon owned by China was spotted in North American airspace, including Alaska, western Canada, and the contiguous United States. On February 4, the U.S. Air Force shot down the balloon over U.S. territorial waters off the coast of South Carolina. Debris from the wreckage was recovered and sent to the FBI Laboratory in Quantico, Virginia, for analysis. Following a preliminary analysis of the debris in June, U.S. officials stated that the balloon carried intelligence gathering equipment but does not appear to have sent information back to China. U.S. president Biden described the balloon as carrying two railroad cars' equivalent of spy equipment; his government said the balloon had a propeller for maneuverability.When the object was first spotted, the Pentagon characterized it as a surveillance balloon. The Chinese government maintained it was a civilian (mainly meteorological) airship that had been blown off course. According to U.S. officials, the balloon carried antennas and other equipment capable of geolocating communications signals, and similar balloons from China have flown over more than 40 nations. Analysts said that its flight path and structural characteristics were dissimilar from those of a typical weather balloon. American officials later disclosed that they had been tracking the balloon since it was launched from Hainan and its original destinations were likely Guam and Hawaii, but prevailing winds blew it off course and across North America.The incident increased U.S.–China tensions. The United States called the balloon's presence a violation of its sovereignty, and its Secretary of State Antony Blinken postponed a long-awaited diplomatic visit to Beijing. Canada summoned the Chinese ambassador in response to the incident.In the United States, three other high-altitude objects, over Northern Alaska (February 10), Yukon (February 11), and Lake Huron (February 11–12) respectively, were detected and subsequently shot down; a later assessment said they had no relation to China.

Background
History and development of reconnaissance balloons
Balloons have been valued for their ability to observe the battlefield and direct artillery. Their usage peaked during World War I, after which they were increasingly replaced by airplanes. During the Cold War, the United States sent hundreds of high-altitude balloons, ostensibly for "meteorological survey" under Project Genetrix, over China and other Eastern Bloc countries to gain intelligence on their nuclear capabilities, drawing their protests.Although mostly supplanted by surveillance satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles, balloons have retained some advantages, such as a lower cost of production and deployment. By 2019, the Pentagon had invested millions in COLD STAR (Covert Long Dwell Stratospheric Architecture), a project for stealthy balloons that are now being transitioned from narcotics surveillance into military service. China recognizes the importance of catching up to foreign countries in this domain. Its military publications have highlighted the use of balloons to assess the early warning and response capabilities of enemy air defenses and to enhance China's own defense capabilities.

Past Chinese balloons and unidentified objects
Suspected Chinese surveillance balloons had been detected in U.S. airspace in the past, namely over Guam, Hawaii, and Florida. One occurred earlier during Joe Biden's presidency (2021–present) and three occurred during Donald Trump's presidency (2017–2021). They did not persist as long as the 2023 incident, and China was able to recover those balloons.Other pre-2023 incursions have remained unexplained, classified by U.S. authorities as unidentified aerial phenomena. In 2022, the Office of the Director for National Intelligence said that there had been at least 171 reports of unexplained aerial phenomena in the United States, and the intelligence community has been unable to determine their precise nature. The commander of United States Northern Command (USNORTHCOM), General Glen VanHerck, said that U.S. failure to detect and identify all such incursions is "a domain awareness gap that we have to figure out". In response the U.S. changed the sensitivity of its radar detection systems, which enabled it to detect additional UFOs.The U.S. Department of State said that a fleet of Chinese balloons have flown over more than forty countries and linked the surveillance activity to the Chinese military. In 2020 and 2021, similar balloons were sighted in Sendai and Hachinohe, Japan respectively, but they were not identified as of Chinese origin at the time. A similar aircraft was sighted in January 2022 over India's strategically important Andaman and Nicobar islands. In February 2022, several balloons were detected off the coast of Taiwan, which their Ministry of National Defense said were likely for meteorological observations for the PLA's Eastern Theater Command. Another crashed near Taiwan in February 2023, carrying an antenna, a transmitter, temperature and humidity sensors, and was likely from China as well.

U.S.–China tensions
The 2023 balloon incident occurred while U.S.–China relations were at their worst in decades, following suspected incidents of Chinese espionage and amid increasing strategic competition in military and economic sectors. In 2022, the United States, along with some of its allies, imposed stringent export controls on "foundational technologies", such as semiconductor microprocessors, to China in order to hamper the latter's development of advanced technology and military tools. The US has also sought to maintain critical supply chains independent from China.

Incident
Balloon
Size, propulsion, and payload
The balloon carried an underslung payload described as a "technology bay" estimated to be the size of "two or three school buses" and was powered by sixteen solar arrays mounted on the payload. The balloon was 200 feet (61 m) tall according to U.S. General Glen D. VanHerck. AI startup Synthetaic, using image data from Planet Labs spacecraft, reported the balloon's diameter as 148 feet (45 m). USNORTHCOM and NORAD Commander, General Glen VanHerck, estimated the payload weighed more than 2,000 pounds (910 kg).The Chinese balloon was a superpressure balloon similar to earlier NASA designs, where the volume of the balloon is kept relatively constant in the face of changes in ambient pressure outside the balloon, and the temperature of the contained lifting gas. This allows better altitude control and much longer endurance compared to the more common variable-volume balloon design.
National Security Council spokesman Admiral John Kirby said the craft had a propeller and could be maneuvered. U.S. officials told foreign diplomats in Beijing that the craft had rudders and propellers. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said it had "limited self-steering capability".The U.S. Department of Defense said the balloon did not present a military or physical threat to people on the ground while it remained in the air, and that shooting it down over water would be safer and increased the opportunity to study the wreckage for intelligence purposes.Citing a PLA procurement portal, a U.S. official said that the balloon was manufactured by a civilian Chinese defense contractor.

Signals intelligence capabilities
Experts noted that weather balloons typically are about 20 feet (6 m) wide, less than a quarter of the balloon's diameter. Those interviewed by BBC News said it was unusual for weather balloons to last as long as the one involved in the incident and that the balloon "might have been more sophisticated than China claims".Images from U-2 flybys and forensic analysis of the payload showed antennas that likely were used for collecting and transmitting signals intelligence. intelligence report has concluded that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman approved the operation to kill journalist Jamal Khashoggi in 2018. The report, released by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, states that the crown prince "approved an operation in Istanbul, Turkey to capture or kill Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi." The report also notes that a team of Saudi operatives, who were part of the crown prince's security detail, carried out the operation. The release of the report has led to calls for accountability and potential sanctions against Saudi Arabia.

**Characters:**

* **Dr. Anya Sharma:** A brilliant climate scientist, passionate about understanding humanity's relationship with the Earth.
* **Leo:** A curious and environmentally conscious high school student.
* **Maya:** Leo's equally bright classmate, with a knack for data analysis.

The hum of the lab was a familiar comfort to Dr. Sharma. Today, however, her gaze was fixed on a complex map projected onto the screen, a mosaic of colors representing Earth's diverse climates. Leo and Maya, their notebooks open, leaned forward intently.

"Alright, team," Dr. Sharma began, her voice clear and engaging. "Today, we’re going to explore a concept that’s crucial for understanding our future: the **human climate niche**."

Leo frowned slightly. "A niche? Like, an ecological niche for a species?"

"Exactly, Leo!" Dr. Sharma beamed. "Just like a polar bear thrives in icy conditions and a cactus in the desert, humans, as a species, have a preferred set of environmental conditions where we’ve historically flourished. That’s our climate niche – the sweet spot of climate conditions that have supported human life and all our activities, like growing food, for millennia."

Maya interjected, "So, it's not just about surviving, but about thriving?"

"Precisely," Dr. Sharma confirmed. "Think of it like a Goldilocks zone for humanity. Not too hot, not too cold, but just right for our complex societies to develop. Now, how do we *estimate* this mysterious niche?" She tapped a stylus on the screen, bringing up a scatter plot.

"We don't have a giant thermometer for all of humanity, do we?" Leo joked.

"Not quite," Dr. Sharma chuckled. "But we have something even better: data! Scientists, over years, have meticulously gathered information on **human population density** across the globe. Then, we correlated that data with the **mean annual temperature** of those regions."

Maya’s eyes lit up. "So, where people are most densely packed, what's the average temperature there?"

"You've got it, Maya!" Dr. Sharma nodded. "When we plot this data – population density against mean annual temperature – a fascinating pattern emerges. It's not a single peak, but a **bimodal distribution**."

She zoomed in on a graph showing two distinct humps. "See here? One prominent peak, or 'mode', appears around **15 degrees Celsius (59°F)**. This represents a huge portion of the global population living in temperate zones, experiencing pleasant springs, warm summers, and moderate winters."

Leo traced the first peak with his finger. "Like much of Europe, parts of North America, and East Asia?"

"Exactly," Dr. Sharma confirmed. "But then, we see another significant hump, a second mode, clustering between **20 to 25 degrees Celsius (68-77°F)**. This represents the vast populations living in warmer, often tropical and subtropical regions."

Maya pondered. "So, humans haven't just adapted to one specific temperature, but two main ranges?"

"That's right," Dr. Sharma explained. "These two modes represent the conditions that have historically allowed for stable agriculture, access to water, and the development of large-scale human settlements. Leo’s brow furrowed. "So, what happens if we step outside this Goldilocks zone?"

Dr. Sharma's expression grew more serious. "That, Leo, is the critical question. With the **rise in mean global temperatures** due to climate change, a significant portion of the human population is projected to experience conditions **beyond our historical climate niche**."

She brought up another projection, a stark visual of red and orange spreading across the globe. "Some models predict that by **2030, 2.0 billion people** will be living in areas outside this comfortable niche. And by **2090, that number could soar to 3.7 billion people** – nearly half of today's global population."

The room fell silent. The sheer scale of those numbers was sobering.

"What does 'out of the niche' even mean?" Maya asked, her voice quiet.

"It means facing unprecedented challenges," Dr. Sharma replied. "Imagine prolonged heatwaves making outdoor work impossible, agricultural land becoming infertile due to drought or extreme heat, increased risk of disease, and displacement of communities. It’s about more than just feeling a bit warmer; it’s about the fundamental systems that sustain us breaking down."

Leo looked up, a glimmer of determination in his eyes. "So, what can we do? Just sit back and watch?"

"Absolutely not!" Dr. Sharma’s voice regained its hopeful tone. "This is where **climate change adaptation** comes in. Adaptation is about being proactive – adjusting to the current and expected effects of climate change. It's about moderating or even avoiding harm, and crucially, exploiting any opportunities that might arise."

"Like building sea walls for rising sea levels?" Maya offered.

"Exactly! Or developing drought-resistant crops, improving early warning systems for extreme weather, designing cooler, more energy-efficient buildings, and even relocating communities in extreme cases," Dr. Sharma elaborated. "Adaptation isn't just for humans; we also need to intervene to help natural systems adjust, like protecting vital ecosystems that provide us with resources."

"So, understanding our climate niche helps us predict where the biggest problems will be, and then adaptation helps us prepare for them?" Leo summarized.

"Precisely, Leo. It's about using scientific understanding to inform our actions," Dr. Sharma concluded. "The human climate niche shows us where we’ve thrived, and the projections show us where we're heading. Adaptation is our roadmap to navigate that future, to protect as many people as possible, and to build a more resilient world. It's a massive challenge, but with knowledge and collective action, it's a challenge we can face."

As the students packed up their notebooks, a new understanding settled upon them. The human climate niche is the ensemble of climate conditions that have sustained human life and human activities, like agriculture, on the globe for the last millennia. The human climate niche is estimated by calculating the human population density with respect to mean annual temperature. The human population distribution as a function of mean annual temperature is bimodal and results in two modes; one at 15 °C and another one at ∼20 to 25 °C. Crops and livestock required for sustaining the human population are also limited to the similar niche conditions. Given the rise in mean global temperatures, the human population is projected to experience climate conditions beyond the human climate niche. Some projections show that considering temperature and demographic changes, 2.0 and 3.7 billion people will live in out of the niche by 2030 and 2090, respectively.

Climate change adaptation is the process of adjusting to the effects of climate change. These can be both current or expected impacts.[1] Adaptation aims to moderate or avoid harm for people. It also aims to exploit opportunities. Humans may also intervene to help adjustment for natural systems.[1] There are many adaptation strategies or options.They can help manage impacts and risks to people and nature.

"Selamat pagi, para penjelajah sinema!" sapa Ibu Sari, guru Bahasa Indonesia yang selalu berhasil membuat pelajaran terasa seperti petualangan. Hari ini, di depan kelas 11 IPA 2, ia memegang sebuah poster film yang didominasi warna tanah dan siluet dua pria dengan topi khas.

"Hari ini, kita akan menyelami kisah 'Gaucho Americano'," lanjutnya, menunjuk poster tersebut. "Film dokumenter Chile yang menarik ini bukan hanya tentang petualangan, tapi juga tentang bagaimana sebuah karya seni memulai perjalanannya, dari ide hingga akhirnya bertemu penonton."

Rudi, siswa yang selalu penasaran, langsung mengangkat tangan. "Bu, saya pernah dengar tentang film ini. Katanya bagus banget, tentang gaucho-gaucho dari Patagonia yang merantau ke Amerika?"

Ibu Sari tersenyum. "Betul sekali, Rudi. 'Gaucho Americano' menceritakan kisah Joaquín dan Víctor, dua gaucho pemberani dari Patagonia Chile. {"final_story": "## The Echoes of Time: A Journey to the Chimnabai Clock Tower

The digital clock on Sarah’s phone pulsed 8:00 AM, a stark contrast to the historical images flashing across the projector screen in Mr. Sharma’s history class. Today’s topic: the architectural gems of India, and specifically, the magnificent Chimnabai Clock Tower in Vadodara.

“Alright class,” Mr. Sharma began, his voice imbued with the usual enthusiasm for the past, “we’re about to embark on a journey back to a time when time itself was a public spectacle, not just a private glance at a device in our pockets.”

He clicked to a vibrant image of the tower – a tall, red-bricked structure with intricate arches and a distinct minaret-like top. “This, students, is the Chimnabai Clock Tower, a masterpiece of Indo-Saracenic architecture. But before we delve into its intricate details, two fundamental questions arise: **When was this grand edifice completed, and who was it named after?**”

Several hands shot up, eager to dive into the research they’d done.

“Anjali, let’s start with you,” Mr. Sharma smiled.

“Sir, the Chimnabai Clock Tower was completed in **1896**,” Anjali announced, her voice clear andconfident. “It says so in all my sources, and it's also mentioned that it was built from funds raised by the citizens of Baroda State.”

“Excellent, Anjali! A critical detail – a community effort, a symbol of public pride. Now, for the second, equally important question: who inspired its name?” Mr. Sharma gestured to Rahul.

Rahul, usually quiet, cleared his throat. “It was named in memory of **Chimnabai I**,” he stated, his eyes fixed on the screen. “She was a queen, the first wife of Sayajirao Gaekwad III, the Maharaja of Baroda State. Her full name was Chimnabai I, and she lived from 1864 to 1885.”

Mr. Sharma nodded approvingly. “Precisely, Rahul. Imagine the profound love and respect Sayajirao must have had for his wife, for such a prominent and lasting tribute to be built in her honor. This tower wasn't just a timekeeper; it was a testament to memory and affection.”

He then continued, painting a vivid picture of the tower's history:

“Construction began well before its completion in 1896, and it quickly became a landmark. You see, back in the late 19th century, public clocks were not just functional; they were statements of progress and civic pride. Create an educational story that helps students understand: When was the Chimnabai Clock Tower completed, and who was it named after?

target_age: "15-18"
story_style: "educational"

Context:
The Chimnabai Clock Tower, also known as the Raopura Tower, is a clock tower situated in the Raopura area of Vadodara, Gujarat, India. It was completed in 1896 and named in memory of Chimnabai I (1864–1885), a queen and the first wife of Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State. It was built in Indo-Saracenic architecture style.

History
Chimnabai Clock Tower was built in 1896. The tower was named after Chimnabai I (1864–1885), a queen and the first wife of Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State. It was inaugurated by Mir Kamaluddin Hussainkhan, the last Nawab of Baroda. During the rule of Gaekwad, it was a stoppage for horse drawn trams. It was constructed from the funds raised by the citizens of Baroda State.The premises of the tower were rented by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation for the last three decades. In 2017, the municipal commissioner, Vinod Rao, ordered to vacate the tower to conserve it as a heritage monument. The mechanical system of the tower clock was replaced by DC motor.

The Chimnabai Clock Tower, also known as the Raopura Tower, is a clock tower situated in the Raopura area of Vadodara, Gujarat, India. It was completed in 1896 and named in memory of Chimnabai I (1864–1885), a queen and the first wife of Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State. It was built in Indo-Saracenic architecture style.

History
Chimnabai Clock Tower was built in 1896. The tower was named after Chimnabai I (1864–1885), a queen and the first wife of Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State. It was constructed from the funds raised by the citizens of Baroda State.The premises of the tower were rented by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation for the last three decades. In 2017, the municipal commissioner, Vinod Rao, ordered to vacate the tower to conserve it as a heritage monument. The mechanical system of the tower clock was replaced by DC motor. The tower is lit up in the evening.

Architecture
The tower was built in Indo-Saracenic architecture style. The five storied tower is built with red bricks. The ground floor has a narrow spiral staircase that leads to upper floors. The first three floors have cusped arched openings decorated with fine stucco work on each side. A huge clock made by John Taylor & Co was brought from London by Sayajirao and fitted to fourth floor. The clock is six feet in diameter and its minute hand is of 3 feet in length. The top floor is octagonal. It has the jharokha with jali-work on all eight sides of the parapet. A steeple stands at the top.

Chimes
During the Gaekwad rule, the mechanical system was used to play tunes every 15 minutes, which later changed to every hour.

{"item_idx": 42, "source": "Myanmar civil war (2021–present)", "language": "id", "question_raw": "Question: What is the current status of the Myanmar civil war, and how many people have been internally displaced since the coup?", "question": "What is the current status of the Myanmar civil war, and how many people have been internally displaced since the coup?", "user_message": "Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What is the current status of the Myanmar civil war, and how many people have been internally displaced since the coup?", "context_type": "v1+v2_merged_dedup", "merged_contexts": ["The Myanmar civil war (Burmese: ၂၀၂၁-၂၀၂၃ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ပြည်သူ့ခုခံတွန်းလှန်စစ်), also called the Myanmar Spring Revolution, and the People's Defensive War, is an ongoing civil war following Myanmar's long-running insurgencies which escalated significantly in response to the 2021 military coup d'état and the subsequent violent crackdown on anti-coup protests.In the months following the coup, the opposition began to coalesce around the National Unity Government, which launched an offensive against the junta. By 2022, the opposition controlled substantial, though sparsely populated, territory. In many villages and towns, the junta's attacks drove out tens of thousands of people. On the second anniversary of the coup, in February 2023, the chairman of the State Administration Council, Min Aung Hlaing, admitted to losing stable control over "more than a third" of townships. Independent observers note the real number is likely far higher, with as few as 72 out of 330 townships and all major population centres remaining under stable control.As of September 2022, 1.3 million people have been internally displaced, and over 13,000 children have been killed. By March 2023, the UN estimated that since the coup, 17.6 million people in Myanmar required humanitarian assistance, while 1.6 million were internally displaced, and 55,000 civilian buildings had been destroyed. UNOCHA said that over 40,000 people fled into neighboring countries.

Background
On the morning of 1 February 2021, the Myanmar military, or Tatmadaw, successfully deposed the elected Myanmar government in a coup, forming a military junta. Former president Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi, and several other members of the National League for Democracy were detained during early morning raids and Min Aung Hlaing was placed as the Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services and de facto ruler of the nation.The exact motives behind the coup are unclear. In the leadup to the coup, the Tatmadaw claimed that the 2020 general elections had 8.6 million voter irregularities, but presented no evidence. The coup may have been a way to re-establish the military's long-reigning power over the country which ended ten years prior.The bloody repression of anti-coup demonstrations led to the creation of armed groups to fight the State Administration Council, the military junta. Gathered under the name of the People's Defence Force (PDF) and the orders of the National Unity Government (NUG), formed by former parliamentarians in office before the coup d'état, the PDF and the NUG officially declared a "defensive war" against the military regime in September 2021. The ACLED estimated that as of 29 July 2022, around 23,521 people in total had been killed in the violence following the 2021 coup.

Existing conflict
Insurgencies have been ongoing in Myanmar since 1948 and have largely been ethnic-based. Communist insurgencies and the Karen National Union were the primary opposition actors to the central government. Over the 20th century, several prominent ethnic armed organisations (EAOs) rose and fell in influence and control. Larger rebel factions such as the Kachin Independence Army formed in response to Ne Win's 1962 Burmese coup d'état and its increased political repression. The 8888 Uprising in response to the totalitarian rule of Ne Win resulted in some of the first modern Bamar militias forming from protestors heading to areas under ethnic rebel control.
In the aftermath of the 8888 Uprising, the State Law and Order Restoration Council, later called the State Peace and Development Council, formed a military junta. The Tatmadaw severely weakened ethnic insurgent groups, destroying most of their bases and strongholds through the 1990s. By the time of the 2011–2015 Myanmar political reforms, the junta had regained control of many long-time rebel strongholds including Kokang and Karen State.As part of its political reforms and democratization, the 2008 Constitution created self-administered zones with increased autonomy. In 2015, the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement (NCA) was signed between 8 EAOs and the central government. However, as soon as 2018, the NCA had already begun to fall apart due to alleged violations of the agreement by Tatmadaw soldiers entering EAO territories to build roads. Many non-signatories continued the conflict. In late 2016, four non-signatories of the NCA formed the Northern Alliance, including the Kachin Independence Army and Arakan Army, engaged in war with the central government and other EAOs.

Prelude
Armed protestors
In late March, dozens of protesters had travelled to Myanmar's border areas to enlist in and train under one of the country's many insurgent groups, elevating the risk of a countrywide civil war. The Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw also proposed the formation of a "federal armed force" to combat the military, and in late March the Arakan Army (AA) threatened to end its ceasefire with the military should the latter "persist in massacring civilians".During late March, protesters increasingly began arming themselves with homemade weapons such as guns in an attempt to defend themselves against attacks by the military. Simultaneously, clashes with soldiers and IED attacks against administrative buildings and police stations became more common as the trend of protesters using armed resistance rose.

Renewed ethnic conflict
The unrest across the nation and the increased need for junta troops in previously peaceful urban areas strengthened EAOs. The Kachin Independence Army (KIA) has already been on the offensive against the military since February and seized the military base of Alaw Bum near the town of Laiza on 25 March. The next day, the Karen National Liberation Army (KNLA) attacked a military base, killing 10 soldiers and taking others hostages in the first attack on the military since the protests began. The following day saw the 2021 Kalay clashes, the first openly armed resistance by protesters in the town of Kalay against the junta. Protestors used homemade weapons against soldiers and security forces attacking a protest camp.The military junta declared that it would cease all military operations on 29 March and hold bilateral negotiations with ethnic armed groups. However, the KIA continued its offensives stating that the Myanmar Army had continued operations as usual. Through April, the informal clashes intensified, such as on 8 April when protesters fought back against soldiers with hunting rifles and firebombs in a battle that resulted in 11 protesters' deaths. The same day, the country surpassed 600 deaths related to anti-coup protests since 1 February.Seven insurgent groups who were signatories to the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement aligned themselves with the Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw, including the All Burma Student Democratic Front and the Karen National Union. The Northern Alliance, comprising the Arakan Army, the Ta'ang National Liberation Army and the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army, attacked a police station in Naungmon, Shan State, killing at least 10 police officers and indicating their disregard of the junta's call for a ceasefire. In response, on 11 April, the junta military launched a counter-attack to recapture the Alaw Bum base using airstrikes and ground troops, but had to retreat amidst heavy casualties.

New conflicts
On 26 April, the Battle of Mindat became one of the first large-scale conflicts arising from the 2021 coup. The Chinland Defense Force (CDF) began armed resistance in Mindat, Chin State. As a response, the junta cut off food and water supplies and declared martial law. Fighting began when a group of demonstrators outside the town's Aung San statue requested the release of six of their arrested colleagues, when a soldier of the regime allegedly fired at someone, prompting protesters to react.

The streets of the town turned into a chaotic battleground, with fires burning and the sound of gunfire echoing through the air.

Despite the overwhelming force of the military, the protesters fought back with whatever they could find. They threw rocks, Molotov cocktails, and set up makeshift barricades to slow down the advancing troops. The clashes continued for hours, with both sides sustaining heavy losses.

The junta, realizing the growing resistance and international pressure, eventually agreed to enter into negotiations with the protesters. A ceasefire was declared, and talks began to find a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the trust between the two sides was shattered, and the road to reconciliation would be long and arduous.

The scars of the conflict would take time to heal, but the people's determination to fight for their rights remained unbroken. **Gelombang Badai di Tanah Emas: Kisah Perang Saudara Myanmar**

Sore itu, di sudut kafe sekolah, Maya dan Rian sedang serius membaca berita di tablet Bima. Topik utamanya adalah konflik di Myanmar. Kening Maya berkerut. "Bima, aku sering dengar tentang Myanmar, tapi konflik ini... sungguh kompleks. Bisa jelaskan apa yang sebenarnya terjadi di sana?"

Bima, yang memang tertarik pada isu-isu sosial-politik, meletakkan bukunya. "Tentu, guys. Bayangkan sebuah negeri yang indah, kaya budaya, yang dijuluki 'Tanah Emas'. Itulah Myanmar. Tapi, di balik keindahannya, ada sejarah panjang gejolak dan perjuangan."

**Awal Mula Badai: Kudeta 2021**

"Inti dari konflik yang sedang berlangsung ini adalah peristiwa yang terjadi pada **1 Februari 2021**," Bima memulai. "Pada pagi itu, Angkatan Bersenjata Myanmar, yang kita sebut Tatmadaw, melakukan **kudeta militer**. Mereka menggulingkan pemerintahan sipil yang terpilih secara demokratis, yang dipimpin oleh Aung San Suu Kyi dan partainya, Liga Nasional untuk Demokrasi (NLD)."

Rian menginterupsi, "Kenapa mereka melakukan itu? Bukankah NLD memenangkan pemilu?"

"Betul sekali," jawab Bima. "Tatmadaw mengklaim ada kecurangan besar dalam pemilu 2020, tapi tidak pernah bisa membuktikannya. Banyak yang meyakini ini adalah upaya Tatmadaw untuk merebut kembali kendali penuh atas negara, setelah sekitar sepuluh tahun kekuasaan sipil yang terbatas."

**Reaksi Rakyat: Dari Protes hingga Perlawanan Bersenjata**

"Tentu saja, rakyat Myanmar tidak tinggal diam," lanjut Bima. "Ribuan orang turun ke jalan, melakukan protes damai menentang kudeta. Tapi, militer merespons dengan kekerasan luar biasa. Penindasan berdarah ini justru memicu sesuatu yang tak terduga."

"Apa itu?" tanya Maya penasaran.

"Protes damai berubah menjadi perlawanan bersenjata," jelas Bima. "Banyak warga sipil yang semula hanya berdemo, mulai mencari cara untuk membela diri. Beberapa pergi ke daerah perbatasan untuk berlatih dengan kelompok-kelompok etnis bersenjata yang sudah bertahun-tahun melawan pemerintah pusat. Lalu, muncullah **Pemerintahan Persatuan Nasional (NUG)**, yang dibentuk oleh anggota parlemen yang digulingkan, dan mereka membentuk **Pasukan Pertahanan Rakyat (PDF)**."

Rian mencatat, "Jadi, PDF ini pasukan perlawanan sipil?"

"Ya, tepat sekali," Bima mengangguk. "Pada September 2021, NUG dan PDF secara resmi menyatakan 'perang defensif' melawan rezim militer. Ini adalah titik balik penting, mengubah protes menjadi perang saudara berskala besar."

**Status Perang Saat Ini: Perebutan Kekuasaan dan Pengungsian Massal**

"Bagaimana situasi perang ini sekarang?" tanya Maya lagi. "Apakah militer masih menguasai segalanya?"

Bima menggeleng. "Tidak lagi. Ini yang menarik, dan sekaligus menyedihkan. Dua tahun setelah kudeta, pada Februari 2023, pemimpin Tatmadaw sendiri, Min Aung Hlaing, mengakui bahwa mereka telah kehilangan kendali stabil atas 'lebih dari sepertiga' dari wilayah perkotaan (township) di Myanmar."

"Wow, itu banyak!" seru Rian.

"Dan pengamat independen percaya angka sebenarnya jauh lebih tinggi," tambah Bima. "Diperkirakan hanya sekitar 72 dari 330 township dan beberapa kota besar saja yang masih dikendalikan penuh oleh junta militer. NUG dan PDF, bersama dengan berbagai **Kelompok Bersenjata Etnis (EAOs)** yang sudah lama ada, kini menguasai sebagian besar wilayah pedesaan, meskipun populasinya tidak padat."

**Dampak Paling Mengenaskan: Pengungsian Internal**

"Lalu, bagaimana nasib rakyat sipil di tengah semua ini?" tanya Maya dengan nada prihatin.

Bima menghela napas. "Inilah bagian yang paling memilukan. Pertempuran sengit, kekerasan militer, dan penyerangan ke desa-desa telah menyebabkan krisis kemanusiaan yang sangat besar. Banyak sekali orang yang terpaksa meninggalkan rumah mereka untuk mencari keselamatan."

"Berapa banyak orang yang diperkirakan mengungsi?" Rian bertanya, melihat ke Bima dengan serius.

"Menurut PBB, pada **Maret 2023**, semenjak kudeta, sekitar **1,6 juta orang telah menjadi pengungsi internal (internally displaced persons/IDPs)** di dalam Myanmar," jelas Bima datar. "Bayangkan, 1,6 juta orang kehilangan rumah, mata pencarian, dan hidup dalam ketidakpastian. Angka ini naik dari 1,3 juta pada September 2022. Selain itu, lebih dari 13.000 anak-anak telah tewas, dan 55.000 bangunan sipil hancur. Bahkan, lebih dari 40.000 orang juga telah melarikan diri ke negara-negara tetangga."

Maya dan Rian terdiam, membayangkan jumlah yang begitu besar.

"Jadi," Rian merangkum, "saat ini Myanmar sedang dilanda perang saudara berskala besar antara junta militer dan pemerintahan sipil NUG bersama PDF serta beberapa EAOs. Junta militer kehilangan kendali signifikan atas sebagian besar wilayah, dan dampaknya, jutaan orang terpaksa mengungsi."

"Tepat sekali," Bima mengangguk. "Ini adalah konflik yang kompleks, dengan akar sejarah panjang pemberontakan etnis, yang semakin diperparah oleh kudeta dan respons brutal militer. Rakyat Myanmar, terutama warga sipil, adalah korban sejati dari Gelombang Badai di Tanah Emas ini. Penting bagi kita untuk terus mengikuti perkembangannya dan memahami perjuangan mereka."

Ketiganya duduk dalam keheningan, merenungkan informasi yang baru mereka dapatkan. Perang saudara di Myanmar adalah pengingat pahit tentang kerapuhan demokrasi dan tingginya harga yang harus dibayar oleh warga sipil ketika perdamaian hilang dari suatu negara.
