{"final_story": "Tentu, mari kita selami kisah memberontaknya Grup Wagner pada tahun 2023, yang bisa kita ibaratkan sebagai "Drama Kekuatan di Balik Layar".

**Judul: Drama Kekuatan di Balik Layar: Pemberontakan Wagner di Tahun 2023**

Para siswa sekalian, bayangkan sebuah panggung besar tempat drama politik dan militer dimainkan. Di sana, tokoh-tokoh kuat bersaing memperebutkan kekuasaan dan pengaruh. Hari ini, kita akan membahas sebuah insiden yang menggemparkan dunia pada bulan Juni 2023: pemberontakan mendadak oleh sebuah kelompok militer swasta bernama Wagner.

**Bab 1: Yevgeny Prigozhin dan Pasukan Bayangan**

Untuk memahami kejadian ini, mari kita kenalan dulu dengan tokoh utamanya: Yevgeny Prigozhin. Bayangkan seorang pengusaha yang lihai, yang dulunya seorang narapidana, lalu bangkit menjadi pemilik restoran-restoran mewah di St. Petersburg, Rusia. Koneksi ini membawanya dekat dengan Presiden Putin.

Pada tahun 2014, Prigozhin mendirikan sesuatu yang disebut "Grup Wagner". Meskipun secara hukum perusahaan militer swasta (PMC) dilarang di Rusia, Wagner beroperasi dengan restu dan dukungan dana pemerintah. Anggap saja Wagner adalah "pasukan bayangan" Rusia. Mengapa? Karena dengan Wagner, pemerintah bisa melakukan operasi militer di berbagai negara (seperti Suriah, Mali, Libya, dan Ukraina) tanpa harus secara resmi mengumumkan keterlibatan langsung atau jumlah korban yang sebenarnya. Ini memungkinkan pemerintah untuk menjaga "tangan bersih" di mata publik.

Wagner terkenal karena kekejamannya dan terlibat dalam konflik di berbagai belahan dunia, bahkan dituduh melakukan kejahatan perang. Mereka juga memiliki jaringan bisnis yang luas di Afrika, mengeksploitasi sumber daya alam sebagai imbalan atas dukungan militer kepada pemerintah setempat. Uang dari bisnis ini kemudian digunakan untuk membiayai operasi Wagner, termasuk di Ukraina.

**Bab 2: Bibit-bibit Ketegangan di Medan Perang Ukraina**

Perang di Ukraina menjadi panggung utama ketegangan. Prigozhin, meskipun mendukung invasi, sering melontarkan kritik pedas kepada Menteri Pertahanan Rusia, Sergei Shoigu, dan Kepala Staf Umum, Valery Gerasimov. Ia menuduh mereka tidak becus memimpin perang dan bahkan menyerahkan "wilayah Rusia" kepada Ukraina.

Bayangkan ini seperti sebuah tim sepak bola: Prigozhin adalah pelatih tim B yang merasa lebih baik, sementara Shoigu dan Gerasimov adalah pelatih tim A yang resmi. Prigozhin percaya bahwa ia lebih efektif dan berani menyuarakan ketidakpuasannya secara terbuka.

Puncaknya terjadi pada pertengahan Juni 2023. Kementerian Pertahanan (MoD) mengeluarkan perintah: semua anggota Wagner harus menandatangani kontrak dengan militer Rusia sebelum 1 Juli. Ini berarti Wagner akan diintegrasikan sepenuhnya ke dalam struktur militer resmi, dan Prigozhin akan kehilangan kendali penuh atas pasukannya serta keuntungan bisnisnya yang menggiurkan, terutama di Afrika.

Prigozhin menolak keras. Ia melihat ini sebagai upaya untuk melemahkan dirinya. Ia bahkan menganjurkan hukuman mati bagi Shoigu dan mengisyaratkan pemberontakan rakyat terhadap pejabat yang tidak kompeten. Prigozhin yakin bahwa jika ia melancarkan pemberontakan, Putin akan mendukungnya, mengingat kedekatan mereka di masa lalu.

**Bab 3: Rencana Pemberontakan dan Kejutan yang Terbongkar**

Badan intelijen Amerika Serikat sebenarnya sudah mencium gelagat tidak beres. Mereka melihat penumpukan pasukan Wagner di dekat perbatasan Rusia dan persiapan logistik. Intelijen Barat juga menemukan rencana ini melalui penyadapan komunikasi dan analisis citra satelit.

Ternyata, Prigozhin telah merencanakan pemberontakan ini jauh sebelum tanggal kejadian. Ia ingin menangkap Menteri Pertahanan Shoigu dan Kepala Staf Umum Gerasimov saat mereka berencana mengunjungi wilayah selatan Rusia yang berbatasan dengan Ukraina. Pejabat Barat mengatakan rencana ini memiliki peluang keberhasilan yang tinggi jika tidak terbongkar.

Namun, dua hari sebelum rencana itu dilaksanakan, Federal Security Service (FSB) Rusia menemukan rencana tersebut. Penemuan ini menyebabkan pemberontakan dimulai lebih cepat dari jadwal, memaksa Prigozhin untuk mengubah rencana dadakan.

Para pejabat AS juga mengungkapkan bahwa Jenderal Angkatan Darat Sergey Surovikin, yang dianggap dekat dengan Prigozhin, ternyata tahu tentang rencana pemberontakan ini. Bahkan, dokumen yang diperoleh CNN menunjukkan bahwa Surovikin memiliki nomor registrasi pribadi dengan Wagner dan keanggotaan VIP rahasia di dalamnya, bersama dengan setidaknya 30 pejabat militer dan intelijen Rusia lainnya. Ini menimbulkan dugaan bahwa ada dukungan dari sebagian kecil petinggi militer untuk pemberontakan tersebut.

**Bab 4: Pecahnya Pemberontakan dan Kemajuan Pesat**

Pada tanggal 23 Juni 2023 malam, Prigozhin menuduh Kementerian Pertahanan melakukan serangan terhadap pasukannya, meskipun klaim ini diragukan. Ini menjadi pemicu deklarasi pemberontakannya. Ia menuntut agar Shoigu dan Gerasimov diserahkan kepadanya.

Pasukan Wagner dengan cepat mengambil alih Rostov-on-Don, sebuah kota penting di selatan Rusia, dan markas besar Distrik Militer Selatan di sana. Kemudian, sebuah konvoi lapis baja Wagner bergerak maju, menuju Moskow, melewati Oblast Voronezh.

Bayangkan adegan ini: konvoi militer swasta bergerak di jalan raya, menembus pertahanan. Mereka dilengkapi dengan sistem anti-pesawat bergerak, yang berhasil menangkis serangan udara militer Rusia. Upaya militer Rusia untuk menghentikan mereka tidak berhasil. Pasukan Wagner terbukti sangat terlatih dan termotivasi. Konsentrasi pertahanan darat Rusia difokuskan di sekitar Moskow.

Presiden Rusia Vladimir Putin dalam pidato televisinya pada 24 Juni, mengutuk tindakan Wagner sebagai pengkhianatan dan berjanji akan menumpas pemberontakan. Situasi sangat tegang, seolah-olah negara berada di ambang perang saudara.

**Bab 5: Akhir yang Tak Terduga dan Penyelamat dari Belarusia**

Namun, sebelum pasukan Wagner mencapai garis pertahanan Moskow, semuanya berubah secara dramatis. Presiden Belarusia, Alexander Lukashenko, memainkan peran kunci. Ia menengahi kesepakatan antara Prigozhin dan Kremlin.

Pada larut malam tanggal 24 Juni, Prigozhin setuju untuk mengakhiri pemberontakan. Pasukan Wagner yang sedang bergerak menuju Moskow berbalik arah, dan mereka yang berada di Rostov-on-Don mulai menarik diri.

**Bab 6: Apa yang Terjadi Selanjutnya?**

Kesepakatan itu termasuk beberapa poin penting:
*   **Kasus Hukum Dicabut:** FSB, yang awalnya membuka kasus pemberontakan bersenjata terhadap Wagner, menutup kasus tersebut pada 27 Juni 2023, membatalkan semua tuduhan. Ini menunjukkan betapa gentingnya situasi dan betapa pentingnya mencapai kesepakatan.
*   **Korban Jiwa:** Setidaknya tiga belas prajurit militer Rusia tewas selama pemberontakan. Di pihak pemberontak, beberapa anggota Wagner terluka dan dua pembelot militer tewas, menurut Prigozhin.
*   **Relokasi Prigozhin dan Wagner:** Sebagai bagian dari kesepakatan, Prigozhin dan beberapa anggota Wagner diizinkan untuk pergi ke Belarusia.

**Kesimpulan: Drama yang Menyimpan Banyak Pertanyaan**

Pemberontakan Wagner di tahun 2023 adalah sebuah peristiwa langka dan mengejutkan yang menunjukkan ketegangan internal yang parah dalam hierarki kekuatan Rusia, terutama di tengah perang yang sedang berlangsung di Ukraina.

**Penyebab utamanya adalah:**
*   **Perang Perebutan Kekuasaan dan Pengaruh:** Prigozhin merasa kekuasaannya terancam oleh upaya MoD untuk mengintegrasikan Wagner ke dalam militer resmi. Ia tidak ingin kehilangan kendali atas pasukan dan bisnisnya yang menguntungkan.
*   **Kritik Terhadap Kepemimpinan Militer:** Ketidakpuasan Prigozhin terhadap kepemimpinan Shoigu dan Gerasimov di Ukraina menjadi pemicu utama. Ia merasa mampu memimpin lebih baik dan menuduh mereka tidak kompeten.
*   **Dukungan yang Salah Duga:** Prigozhin mungkin salah mengira bahwa ia akan mendapatkan dukungan yang lebih besar dari elemen-elemen dalam struktur kekuasaan Rusia, atau bahwa Putin akan memihaknya.

**Bagaimana pemberontakan ini berakhir?**
*   Melalui **mediasi darurat** oleh Presiden Belarusia, Alexander Lukashenko, yang berhasil mencapai kesepakatan dengan Prigozhin.

On 23 June 2023, the Wagner Group, a Russian government-funded paramilitary and private military company, staged a rebellion after a period of increasing tensions between the Russian Ministry of Defence and the leader of Wagner, Yevgeny Prigozhin. An agreement to settle this conflict was reached between the two sides the next day, 24 June 2023.
While Prigozhin was supportive of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, he had previously publicly criticized Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov, blaming them for the country's military shortcomings and accusing them of handing over "Russian territories" to Ukraine. Prigozhin portrayed the rebellion as a response to an alleged attack on his forces by the ministry, and demanded that Shoigu and Gerasimov be turned over to him. In a televised address on 24 June, Russian president Vladimir Putin denounced Wagner's actions as treason and pledged to quell the rebellion.
Prigozhin's forces took control of Rostov-on-Don and the headquarters of the Southern Military District in the city. An armored column of Wagner troops advanced through Voronezh Oblast towards Moscow. Armed with mobile anti-aircraft systems, the rebels repelled the air attacks of the Russian military, whose actions did not deter the progress of the column. Ground defenses were concentrated on the approach to Moscow. Before Wagner reached the defenses, Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko brokered a settlement with Prigozhin, who agreed to end the rebellion. On the late evening of 24 June, Wagner forces turned around, and those that had remained in Rostov-on-Don began withdrawing.
As per the agreement, the Federal Security Service, which had initiated a case for armed rebellion under Article 279 of the Criminal Code closed the case on 27 June 2023, dropping the charges. At least thirteen servicemen of the Russian military were killed during the rebellion. On the rebels' side, several Wagner members were reported injured and two military defectors were killed according to Prigozhin.

Background
Yevgeny Prigozhin and the Wagner Group
In the early 2000s, Prigozhin, having served a decade in prison before embarking on an entrepreneurial path, emerged as a prominent figure in Saint Petersburg's business landscape, gaining recognition for a string of highly regarded restaurants. This connection eventually facilitated a financial association with Putin, who was actively engaged in municipal politics during that period. Prigozhin gradually evolved into a trusted and intimate confidant of Putin, forging a close personal bond.In 2014, Prigozhin founded the Wagner Group, a Russian private military company. Despite the legal prohibition of private military companies in Russia, Wagner operated unimpeded with implicit endorsement and funding from the Russian government. Many analysts have said that the government employed Wagner services to allow for plausible deniability and to obscure the actual toll in terms of casualties and financial costs of Russia's foreign interventions.Serving as a tool of Russian foreign and military policy, Wagner emerged as a formidable combat force in various regions, including the Donbas conflict. It played a significant role during Russia's military intervention in the Syrian civil war, providing support to Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, and has participated in conflicts in Mali, Libya, and the Central African Republic. Wagner has garnered infamy due to its ruthless methods and its participation in war crimes throughout Africa, the Middle East, and Ukraine, perpetrating atrocities with impunity.The group maintains close ties with multiple African governments, enjoying considerable autonomy to exploit the natural resources of these nations in return for supporting local forces in their battle against anti-government rebels. Wagner's economic endeavors in Africa witnessed an upward trajectory even amidst the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as the funds generated were channeled towards financing the conflicts in Ukraine and other regions.

Order to integrate Wagner
In mid-June 2023, the MoD ordered Wagner to sign contracts with the military before 1 July. This move effectively integrated Wagner as a subordinate unit within the regular command structure, thereby diminishing the influence of Prigozhin. However, Prigozhin declined to sign the agreement, alleging incompetence on the part of Shoigu. Reports from the independent Russian news outlet Meduza indicated that this development would undermine Prigozhin's hold over Wagner and jeopardize the group's profitable operations in Africa. Prigozhin unsuccessfully attempted to circumvent the order for Wagner's subordination while intensifying his criticism of the MoD. He went as far as advocating for the execution of Shoigu and hinting at a potential popular uprising against inept officials. Prigozhin believed that Putin would ultimately side with him in his struggle against the MoD if he launched a mutiny.

Planning the rebellion
U.S. intelligence agencies observed a gradual accumulation of Wagner forces near the Russian border along with evidence of Wagner stockpiling equipment and resources in preparation for the rebellion. Although they obtained information regarding the where and how of the planned rebellion, the exact timing remained unknown. Western intelligence agencies reportedly uncovered the plan through communications intercepts and satellite image analysis. Several weeks prior to the actual event, U.S. intelligence started foreseeing a significant Wagner insurrection and obtained solid evidence of the imminent rebellion before 21 June. Prigozhin seemed to have set the plan in motion following the MoD decision on 10 June, which would effectively integrate Wagner forces into the regular military. Surovikin had acted as an intermediary between Prigozhin and the military hierarchy and was perceived to have close ties to Prigozhin. CNN obtained documents that indicated Surovikin had a personal registration number with Wagner and held a covert VIP membership within the group, alongside at least 30 other high-ranking Russian military and intelligence officials. Additionally, there were indications that other generals may have lent their support to the uprising. The discovery of the plan led to the premature start of the rebellion. ## Petualangan di Dunia Pangan Masa Depan: Mengenal Gigi dan FoodFutureCo

Langit di atas kafe itu cerah, secerah semangat tiga sahabat yang sedang asyik berdiskusi. Ada Anya yang gemar sekali mencoba resep-resep baru dari seluruh dunia, Budi yang selalu ingin tahu bagaimana makanan bisa sampai ke piring kita, dan Candra yang punya impian besar untuk membantu menyelamatkan bumi lewat makanan.

“Kalian tahu tidak,” mulai Anya, sambil menyeruput *matcha latte*-nya, “Aku baru saja membaca artikel menarik tentang masa depan pangan. Ada perusahaan namanya FoodFutureCo.”

Budi menaikkan alisnya penasaran, “FoodFutureCo? Kedengarannya seperti film fiksi ilmiah! Apa itu?”

Candra, yang memang sering mencari tahu tentang inovasi berkelanjutan, menyahut, “Oh, aku juga pernah dengar! Itu semacam ‘akselerator’ untuk bisnis makanan, kan? Tapi bedanya, mereka fokus pada perusahaan yang tidak hanya mau untung, tapi juga punya tujuan mulia, atau yang mereka sebut ‘*purpose-driven*’.”

“Tepat sekali!” seru Anya. “Dan yang lebih menarik, Managing Director-nya adalah seorang wanita luar biasa bernama **Gigi Lee Chang**.”

“Managing Director?” tanya Budi. “Itu seperti kepala perusahaan, ya?”

“Kurang lebih begitu,” jawab Candra. “Dia adalah orang di balik kemudi yang memastikan FoodFutureCo berjalan sesuai visinya. Dan yang spesial dari FoodFutureCo ini, mereka tidak bekerja dengan *startup* yang baru mulai. Sebaliknya, mereka membantu perusahaan makanan yang sudah punya produk, sudah punya pendapatan, dan siap untuk berkembang lebih besar lagi.”

Anya membuka tabletnya, “Begini, FoodFutureCo itu didirikan oleh Shen Tong pada tahun 2016. Tujuannya sederhana: membantu perusahaan-perusahaan pangan yang punya dampak positif, seperti di bidang *agtech* (teknologi pertanian), makanan nabati, makanan laut berkelanjutan, sampai pengurangan sisa makanan. Mereka menyebutnya sebagai ‘akselerator *scale-up*’.”

“Jadi, bukan cuma sekadar ingin jualan, tapi juga ingin memberi dampak baik pada lingkungan dan masyarakat?” tanya Budi, mulai memahami.

“Persis!” kata Candra. “Dan Gigi Lee Chang adalah sosok kunci yang membuat semua itu terjadi.”

“Apa saja sih yang sudah dilakukan Gigi Lee Chang sampai dia jadi Managing Director sebuah perusahaan keren seperti FoodFutureCo?” tanya Anya, penasaran.

Candra tersenyenyum. “Dia bukan orang sembarangan. Gigi Lee Chang bahkan pernah disebut oleh majalah Forbes sebagai salah satu dari delapan wanita yang memimpin masa depan pangan di dunia. Keren, kan?”

Budi mengangguk setuju. “Hebat sekali!”

“Prestasinya banyak sekali,” lanjut Anya, membaca lagi artikel di tabletnya. “Pertama, dia adalah **pendiri Plum Organics**. Ada yang tahu Plum Organics?”

Candra berpikir sebentar. “Sepertinya pernah dengar. Itu merek makanan bayi organik, kan?”

“Betul sekali!” Anya mengacungkan jempol. “Bayangkan, dia melihat peluang untuk menyediakan makanan bayi yang sehat dan organik, dan dia berhasil membangun perusahaan itu hingga sukses. Ini menunjukkan visinya yang tajam dan kemampuannya membangun sesuatu dari nol.”

“Dan itu bukan satu-satunya pencapaiannya,” tambah Candra. “Gigi juga pernah menjabat sebagai **CEO organisasi nirlaba Healthy Child Healthy World**. Organisasi ini fokus pada kesehatan anak dan lingkungan.”

“Wah, dari bisnis ke nirlaba!” Budi kagum. “Itu berarti dia peduli sekali dengan isu sosial dan kesehatan, ya?”

“Tentu,” jawab Anya. “Selain itu, dia juga memberikan nasihat kepada **B Lab**, sebuah organisasi nirlaba yang mendukung perusahaan-perusahaan yang punya dampak sosial dan lingkungan positif, yang sering disebut B Corp. Jadi, dia tidak hanya membangun bisnisnya sendiri, tapi juga membantu orang lain untuk membangun bisnis yang bertanggung jawab.”

“Jadi, intinya, Gigi Lee Chang ini adalah seorang pemimpin yang sangat berpengalaman di industri makanan,” simpul Candra. “Dia tahu betul bagaimana membangun bisnis yang sukses, dan dia juga sangat peduli dengan dampak positif yang bisa dihasilkan melalui makanan.”

Anya menambahkan, “Betul. Dia dan pendiri FoodFutureCo, Shen Tong, adalah nama-nama besar di lingkungan investor makanan berkelanjutan. Mereka sering menjadi pembicara di berbagai konferensi dan summit penting, seperti FoodTank, Future of Food Summit, dan Women in Green. Ini menunjukkan pengaruh mereka yang besar dalam membentuk arah masa depan pangan.”

“Aku jadi penasaran, apa yang membuat FoodFutureCo itu unik di antara akselerator lainnya?” tanya Budi.

Anya menyeringai. “Gigi Lee Chang sendiri yang menjelaskan. Katanya ada tiga hal yang membuat mereka tidak biasa:
1.  **Ekosistem yang sangat luas:** Mereka tidak hanya fokus pada satu area saja, tapi melihat seluruh rantai pasok makanan, dari pertanian sampai ke piring.
2.  **Fokus pada perusahaan yang punya misi dan tujuan:** Mereka hanya bekerja dengan perusahaan yang ingin membuat perbedaan positif di dunia.
3.  **Tidak mencari *startup*:** Mereka bekerja dengan perusahaan yang sudah mapan dan siap ‘naik level’, bukan yang baru merintis.”

“Pantas saja perusahaan-perusahaan yang mereka bantu seperti Plum Organics punya potensi besar,” kata Budi. “Dengan bimbingan dari seseorang seperti Gigi Lee Chang, pasti perusahaan-perusahaan dalam *cohort* FoodFutureCo bisa berkembang pesat.”

“Betul,” Candra mengiyakan. “Setiap *cohort* itu berjalan selama 4 bulan. Perusahaan-perusahaan di dalamnya mendapatkan program yang disesuaikan, dengan bimbingan dan nasihat dari para ahli dan jaringan investor yang luas. Mereka membantu dari peningkatan keterlibatan konsumen sampai pesan merek yang lebih jelas.”

Anya menegakkan badannya, matanya berbinar. “Aku jadi punya inspirasi! Kita tidak hanya bisa menikmati makanan, tapi juga bisa menjadi bagian dari perubahan positif di dunia pangan, seperti Gigi Lee Chang. Mungkin suatu hari nanti, kita juga bisa menciptakan inovasi di bidang makanan yang memberikan dampak baik.”

Budi dan Candra mengangguk setuju. Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: Who is the Managing Director of FoodFutureCo and what are some of her accomplishments in the food industry?

target_age: "15-18"

Context:
FoodFutureCo is a scale-up accelerator for purpose-driven food businesses. FoodFutureCo was founded by Shen Tong, American social activist and investor in 2016 to support post-revenue food companies who are primed to expand from early adoption to early majority. The accelerator program works with companies in agtech, agriculture, consumer packaged goods, local & plant-based foods, sustainable seafood, restaurant concepts, and food waste. The handful of companies within each cohort are established yet small companies with massive skill potential.  
Managing Director of FoodFutureCo is Gigi Lee Chang, profiled as one of eight women leading the future of food by Forbes. She founded Plum Organics, was the CEO of the nonprofit Healthy Child Healthy World, and advised the nonprofit B Lab. {"final_story": "The classroom buzzed with the usual Friday afternoon energy, but a hushed anticipation fell as Mr. Sharma switched on the projector. "Today, we're going to explore a real-life event, a tragic one, but one that offers incredible insights into the complexities of aviation and human factors," he began, his voice calm but serious. "We're going to talk about Yeti Airlines Flight 691."

A few students shifted, some eyes widening. They remembered the headlines, the images from that grim day in January 2023.

"On January 15th, 2023," Mr. Sharma continued, "Yeti Airlines Flight 691, an ATR 72 aircraft, took off from Kathmandu, bound for Pokhara, Nepal. It was a domestic flight, a routine hop. But as it approached Pokhara International Airport, something went terribly wrong. All 72 people on board perished, making it the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72."

He displayed an image of the modern Pokhara International Airport, opened just two weeks before the crash. "The aircraft was moments from landing. A video filmed from the ground showed it banking steeply to the left, then plummeting into the Seti Gandaki River. Another, even more chilling video, was live-streamed by a passenger, seconds before impact."

A collective gasp went through the room. Mr. Sharma acknowledged it with a solemn nod. "It's hard to imagine the fear, the suddenness of it all. But our goal isn't just to remember the tragedy, it's to understand *why* it happened, so we can learn from it and hopefully prevent future incidents."

He moved to a new slide with a diagram of an aircraft cockpit. "Let's dive into the investigation. When an accident like this occurs, a team of experts is immediately formed. They gather every single piece of evidence – from wreckage to flight data recorders and cockpit voice recorders. Think of these as the aircraft's 'black boxes,' recording everything the plane did and everything the pilots said."

"In this case," Mr. Sharma explained, "the crash happened on a clear day. Initially, there were speculations about a technical issue. Flightradar24, an online flight tracker, data even showed inaccurate speed and altitude readings at one point, which was unusual. But the real story began to unfold when the black boxes were analyzed."

He clicked to a simplified diagram of an ATR 72's engine controls. "Now, this is where it gets highly technical, but crucial. An ATR 72 is a turboprop aircraft. It uses propellers to generate thrust. These propellers aren't just one-speed, like a fan. They have a subtle but vital control called the 'condition lever.' This lever controls the angle of the propeller blades, and a specific position, 'feathered,' means the blades are angled to reduce drag when an engine is off or malfunctioning. When feathered, the propellers don't produce thrust, even if the engine itself is running. It's like putting a car in neutral and trying to accelerate."

He paused, letting the information sink in. "The preliminary report from the investigation revealed something startling. Roughly a minute before the crash, the aircraft's propellers for *both* engines went into the feathered condition."

A student, Akash, raised his hand. "So, the propellers weren't pushing air anymore? Even though the engines were probably turning?"

"Exactly, Akash!" Mr. Sharma affirmed. "The Flight Data Recorder, or FDR, showed that the propeller rotation speed dropped drastically, and the torque – the rotational force – went to zero. This means the aircraft was gliding, losing speed, and plummeting towards a stall, which is when the wings can no longer generate enough lift to keep the plane in the air."

He displayed a screenshot of the cockpit layout, highlighting where the condition levers and flap levers are located. "Here's the critical part: in the ATR 72, the condition levers are located very close to the flap levers. Flaps are movable sections on the wings that increase lift, crucial for slowing down and landing. The pilots, during the approach, absolutely needed to extend the flaps."

"The Cockpit Voice Recorder, or CVR, captured the communication: The flying pilot (PF) called for 'FLAPS 30.' The monitoring pilot (PM) responded, 'Flaps 30 and descending.' However, the FDR showed no flap movement at that exact moment. Instead, the propellers began to feather."

"The investigators speculate that the monitoring pilot, perhaps intending to move the flap lever, inadvertently moved the *condition levers* into the feathered position instead. Imagine reaching for the brake pedal and accidentally hitting the accelerator in a critical moment, though this analogy isn't perfect, it conveys the idea of an unintended action with severe consequences."

"For an agonizing minute, the aircraft was essentially flying without thrust. The pilots realized they lacked power. The CVR recorded the flying pilot saying twice, 'there was no power coming from the engines.' They advanced the power levers to maximum, but it made no difference because the propellers were feathered."

"What’s even more tragic is that about twenty seconds after the initial mistake, the monitoring pilot *did* set the flaps correctly. But by then, the crucial error of feathering the propellers had been made and remained uncorrected. The pilots, under immense pressure and perhaps focused on other aspects of landing, didn’t recognize that the condition levers were in the wrong position. This indicates that the pre-landing checklist, a vital safety procedure, was likely not properly followed at that critical moment."

"So, what caused the crash of Yeti Airlines Flight 691?" Mr. Sharma looked at the class. "It wasn't a single catastrophic failure, but a chain of events, a tragic sequence of human errors compounded by the close proximity of critical controls and the high-pressure environment of landing."

He summarized:
1.  **Inadvertent Actuation:** The monitoring pilot likely mistakenly moved the condition levers to the feathered position instead of the flap lever.
2.  **Loss of Thrust:** With the propellers feathered, the engines generated no thrust, causing the aircraft to lose airspeed and altitude rapidly.
3.  **Lack of Awareness:** The pilots, despite noticing the lack of engine power, failed to identify that the condition levers were in the feathered position.
4.  **Inadequate Checklist Adherence:** The critical pre-landing checklist was not followed precisely, which could have identified the error.
5.  **Aviation Dynamics:** Without thrust, the aircraft stalled, leading to the rapid loss of control captured in the ground video.

"This accident is a somber reminder of several key principles in aviation safety," Mr. Sharma concluded. "The importance of rigorous training, the role of clear cockpit design to prevent confusion, and the absolute necessity of following checklists, especially in complex, high-stakes situations. Every element, from the smallest switch to the most experienced pilot, plays a part in the intricate dance of safe flight. And when something goes wrong, it’s rarely just one thing, but a confluence of factors."

The bell rang, but the usual rush was absent. Create an educational story that helps students understand: What caused the crash of Yeti Airlines Flight 691 in Pokhara, Nepal?

target_age: "15-18"
story_style: "educational"
language: "English"

Context:
Yeti Airlines Flight 691 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara in Nepal. On 15 January 2023, the aircraft being operated on the route, an ATR 72 flown by Yeti Airlines, crashed while landing at Pokhara, killing all 72 occupants on board. It is the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.

Accident
The flight took off from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport at 10:33 am NST. It crashed on the bank of the Seti Gandaki River while on final approach to landing at Pokhara International Airport. A video filmed from the ground showed the aircraft banking steeply to the left before crashing 65 metres (213 ft) away. Another video was streamed live on Facebook by Sonu Jaiswal, a passenger on the plane, before and during the crash. The video shows passengers unaware of the situation until seconds before impact.The crash occurred in Gandaki Province between the old Pokhara Airport and the new Pokhara International Airport, which was opened two weeks earlier and also where the aircraft was intending to land. The accident resulted in the deaths of all 72 people on board, and was Nepal's worst aviation accident since the crash of Pakistan International Airlines Flight 268 in 1992, the deadliest aviation accident in Nepalese domestic aviation, and the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.According to an official at the Pokhara International Airport, air traffic control cleared the flight to land on runway 30 heading from east to west, but the captain requested the opposing runway 12 heading from west to east, minutes before the crash. A Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal spokesperson said: "The weather was clear; according to preliminary information the cause of the crash is the technical issue of the plane."Flight-tracking organisation Flightradar24 noted that during the flight the aircraft had been transmitting inaccurate speed and altitude data.

Aftermath
The airport was closed as authorities launched a rescue operation. The Government of Nepal summoned an emergency cabinet meeting following the crash. Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal said he was deeply saddened by the tragic accident. The Office of the Prime Minister declared 16 January to be a national day of mourning, and the flag of Nepal was flown at half-staff. Yeti Airlines cancelled all regular flights scheduled for the day.

Investigation
Experts noted that the video from the ground taken moments before the crash showed the aircraft's nose noticeably high before the left wing suddenly dropped, probably indicating a stall. Hours after the crash, a five-member committee headed by Nagendra Ghimire was set up to investigate the accident in conjunction with the French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety.
On 16 January, the flight data and cockpit voice recorders were found; the recorders were examined in Singapore and with assistance from Transportation Safety Board of Canada, Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety, and Transport Safety Investigation Bureau of Singapore. About a month later, on 13 February, a preliminary report was released, which largely reproduced all relevant logs:At 10:56:27, the PF disengaged the Autopilot System (AP) at an altitude of 721 feet Above Ground Level (AGL). The PF then called for "FLAPS 30" at 10:56:32, and the PM replied, "Flaps 30 and descending". The flight data recorder (FDR) data did not record any flap surface movement at that time. Instead, the propeller rotation speed (Np) of both engines decreased simultaneously to less than 25% and the torque (Tq) started decreasing to 0%, which is consistent with both propellers going into the feathered condition...
The flight crew then carried out the "Before Landing Checklist" before starting the left turn onto the base leg. During that time, the power lever angle increased from 41% to 44%. At the point, Np of both propellers were recorded as Non-Computed Data (NCD) in the FDR and the torque (Tq) of both engines were at 0%. When propellers are in feather, they are not producing thrust...
At 10:56:54, another click was heard, followed by the flaps surface movement to the 30 degrees position.

When ATC gave the clearance for landing at 10:57:07, the PF mentioned twice that there was no power coming from the engines. At 10:57:11, the power levers were advanced first to 62 degrees then to the maximum power position. At 10:57:20, the PM (who was previously the PF) repeated again that there was no power from the engines...
The aircraft's propellers had been feathered for a minute prior to the crash, causing the engine to produce no thrust and lead the vehicle into a stall; the condition levers, which control the propellers, were discovered from the wreckage set to the feathered position. Seconds preceding the crash, the pilots discussed a total lack of power and even moved the power lever to the extreme but failed to recognize that the condition levers were wrongly set. That the condition levers and the flap lever are next to each other in an ATR 72, experts speculate that the monitoring pilot (Kamal KC) had inadvertently moved the former in place of the latter, when asked of by the flying pilot; while, about twenty seconds later, he would set the flap lever properly on his own, he failed to account for his previous mistake, implying that the landing checklist was not properly followed.

Langit malam di Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, India, selalu memiliki daya tarik tersendiri bagi Arya. Sebagai seorang siswa SMA yang terobsesi dengan teknologi luar angkasa, setiap peluncuran roket adalah sebuah peristiwa besar baginya. 'SpaceExplorer', anggota lain yang tampaknya sangat berpengetahuan, menambahkan detailnya. "Peluncuran akan dilakukan pada **pukul 06:30 IST (Indian Standard Time)**. An agreement to settle this conflict was reached between the two sides the next day, 24 June 2023.
While Prigozhin was supportive of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, he had previously publicly criticized Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov, blaming them for the country's military shortcomings and accusing them of handing over "Russian territories" to Ukraine. Prigozhin portrayed the rebellion as a response to an alleged attack on his forces by the ministry, and demanded that Shoigu and Gerasimov be turned over to him. In a televised address on 24 June, Russian president Vladimir Putin denounced Wagner's actions as treason and pledged to quell the rebellion.
Prigozhin's forces took control of Rostov-on-Don and the headquarters of the Southern Military District in the city. An armored column of Wagner troops advanced through Voronezh Oblast towards Moscow. Armed with mobile anti-aircraft systems, the rebels repelled the air attacks of the Russian military, whose actions did not deter the progress of the column. Ground defenses were concentrated on the approach to Moscow. Before Wagner reached the defenses, Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko brokered a settlement with Prigozhin, who agreed to end the rebellion. On the late evening of 24 June, Wagner forces turned around, and those that had remained in Rostov-on-Don began withdrawing.
As per the agreement, the Federal Security Service, which had initiated a case for armed rebellion under Article 279 of the Criminal Code closed the case on 27 June 2023, dropping the charges. At least thirteen servicemen of the Russian military were killed during the rebellion. On the rebels' side, several Wagner members were reported injured and two military defectors were killed according to Prigozhin.

Background
Yevgeny Prigozhin and the Wagner Group
In the early 2000s, Prigozhin, having served a decade in prison before embarking on an entrepreneurial path, emerged as a prominent figure in Saint Petersburg's business landscape, gaining recognition for a string of highly regarded restaurants. This connection eventually facilitated a financial association with Putin, who was actively engaged in municipal politics during that period. Prigozhin gradually evolved into a trusted and intimate confidant of Putin, forging a close personal bond.In 2014, Prigozhin founded the Wagner Group, a Russian private military company. **Dr. Thorne:** These "ticks" are thought to have experienced mass wasting events, like enormous landslides, along their margins. Sometimes you can even see the debris scattered around them. It's a testament to the powerful geological forces at play on Venus.

But recent evidence has painted a much more exciting picture.

**(Dr. Thorne brings up a series of radar images.)**

**Liam:** So, like, actual eruptions?

**Dr. Thorne:** Very likely! And the evidence just keeps mounting. In 2020, studies of Venus's coronae – those large, circular features – revealed that 37 of them show signs of ongoing activity. As one scientist put it, "these are not ancient volcanoes, but ones that are active today, dormant perhaps, but not dead."

**Maya:** That's incredible! So, we're talking about active volcanism *now*?

**Dr. Thorne:** Even more recently, Maya, in March 2023, scientists announced direct proof. They re-examined old Magellan orbiter data from the early 1990s. By comparing radar images taken 8 months apart, they found that a volcanic vent in the Maat Mons region had expanded by almost 2 square kilometers! Computer simulations confirmed that this change couldn't be explained by imaging angles, meaning it had to be a structural change caused by active volcanism.

**Liam:** So, we finally have proof! Venus is still erupting!

**Dr. Thorne:** Indeed! It’s a monumental discovery. And it opens up a whole new understanding of this enigmatic planet.

**Maya:** What about lightning? I heard that lightning can be a sign of volcanic activity on Earth.

**Dr. Thorne:** Another excellent point, Maya. On Earth, volcanic plumes can generate lightning. On Venus, however, directly observing lightning is incredibly challenging due to its thick, sulfuric acid clouds. These clouds scatter and absorb light, making it difficult to spot any faint flashes.

**Liam:** So, no lightning on Venus then?

**Dr. Thorne:** Not necessarily no lightning, Liam, but no *direct* observations yet. **Liam:** And can we bring some heat-resistant marshmallows?

Amini had been arrested by the Guidance Patrol for allegedly violating Iran's mandatory hijab law by wearing her hijab "improperly" while visiting Tehran from Saqqez. According to eyewitnesses, she had been severely beaten by Guidance Patrol officers, an assertion denied by Iranian authorities. As the protests spread from Amini's hometown of Saqqez to other cities in the Iranian Kurdistan and throughout Iran, the government responded with widespread Internet blackouts, nationwide restrictions on social media usage, tear gas and gunfire.Although the protests have not been as deadly as those in 2019 (when more than 1,500 were killed), they have been "nationwide, spread across social classes, universities, the streets [and] schools", and called the "biggest challenge" to the government of Iran since the Islamic Revolution in 1979. At least 537 people, including 68 minors, had been killed as a result of the government's intervention in the protests, as of 4 April 2023.  An estimated 19,262 have been arrested throughout at least 134 cities and towns, and at 132 universities.Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei dismissed the widespread unrest not only as "riots" but also as a "hybrid war" caused by foreign states and dissidents abroad. Women, including schoolchildren, have played a key role in the demonstrations. In addition to demands for increased rights for women, the protests have demanded the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, setting them apart from previous major protest movements in Iran, which have focused on election results or economic woes. 
The government's response to the protests has been widely condemned.

Historical background
Since shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Iranian women have been legally required to completely cover their hair in public with a hijab. Enforcement of the unpopular law was eased during the 2013–2021 tenure of President Rouhani, but was then intensified under Rouhani's successor, the hard-line President Ebrahim Raisi.  Bloody Aban  (Persian: آبان خونین), a month near November in the Iranian calendar, was a series of 2019 protests initially caused by a 50–200% increase in fuel prices, and as part of the wider Iranian Democracy Movement, leading to calls for the overthrow of the government in Iran and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

Mahsa Amini's arrest and death in custody
Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman, was arrested by the Guidance Patrol on 14 September 2022 because of an "improper hijab." The police were accused of beating her and inflicting a fatal head injury; Amini was pronounced dead on 16 September. After a CT scan confirmed that Amini had sustained head injuries, the head of the Guidance Patrol was allegedly suspended, a claim that was denied by Tehran police.

Protests
Initial protests, mostly led by women, demanded an end to the mandatory hijab; these protests evolved into a national revolt. The protests became more widespread than those of 2009, 2017, and 2019, encompassing even Islamic Republic power bases such as the holy cities of Mashhad and Qom. Unlike some previous protests, the new protests involved both urban middle classes and rural working areas. In addition, schoolgirls demonstrated in numbers for the first time. While continuing to protest Amini's death and demanding an end to the mandatory hijab, Iranians also advocated for wider freedoms and women's rights, and protested against the morality police, the Ayatollah, and the theocratic regime.Unlike many previous Iranian protests, protesters appear to be demanding a wholesale change in government rather than limiting themselves to incremental reforms. In a November 2022 Group for Analyzing and Measuring Attitudes in Iran (GAMAAN) poll, almost three-quarters of Iranians opposed mandatory hijab; of these anti-hijabis, 84% would prefer a secular Iranian state to theocracy, which GAMAAN characterized as an endorsement of regime change. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, economic hardship and poor living conditions contributed to the growth of the protests. The New York Times itemized Iranian grievances such as "soaring prices, high unemployment, corruption, (and) political repression", and identified the poor Iranian economy as a major force behind the protests; according to an Iranian report in August 2021, a third of Iranians live in poverty. Abdolreza Davari, a conservative analyst, has quoted a statistic that 95 percent of Iranians are "worried about their livelihoods today and for their and their children's future." Only 15% of Iranians in the job market are women. Iran ranked 143rd out of 146 countries in the 2022 WEF Gender Gap Report, due in part to prohibitions on female membership in powerful government organizations.In response to the protests, people held demonstrations in support of the government across several cities in Iran, in an attempt to counter the protests. The Iranian government referred to these counter-protests as "spontaneous". The pro-government protesters called for the anti-government protesters to be executed, and referred to them as "Israel's soldiers" whilst shouting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel", reflecting Iran's clerical rulers' usual narrative of putting the blame of the unrest on foreign countries.Media coverage was constrained by Iranian restrictions on speech, including Internet shutdowns and arrests of journalists. NBC News retained a correspondent in Tehran. Most Western outlets obtained information from networks of contacts, human rights groups, and social media content. According to BBC News, an Iranian government disinformation campaign produced social media videos and fake interviews, and attempted to trick Western media into reporting falsehoods: "They can then say foreign media is reporting fake news".According to France 24, protests "had dwindled" across most of the country by March 2023.

Events of chain poisoning in girls' schools occurred.
The state began a surveillance program.

Actions by protesters
Protesters often stage small and quick, but numerous, "flash mob" gatherings. Drivers have blocked streets with their cars to slow down security forces; roads have also been blocked by dumpster bins or even overturned police cars. Security forces on motorbikes cut through traffic, with passengers firing on protesters. In some cases security forces used paintballs to mark demonstrators; some demonstrators packed extra clothes to replace painted clothes, wore masks to avoid identification, or dismantled public security cameras. Some protesters chanted from windows or rooftops. Symbolic protests include dyeing fountains blood-red, and women discarding and burning their hijabs or cutting their hair in public. Since turbans are viewed as a symbol of the regime, some activists engaged in turban throwing (knocking the turbans off of "privileged" Iranian clerics on the street and running away); reformers such as Ahmad Zaidabadi criticized the trend, and said the practice can harass uninvolved scholars.

Civil boycotts
Some university teachers and professors declared their support for the student movement by boycotting classes or resigning. They included Nasrollah Hekmat (Shahid Beheshti University), Ammar Ashoori (Islamic Azad University), Lili Galehdaran (Shiraz Art University) and Gholamreza Shahbazi (Art and Soureh Universities), together with Alireza Bahraini, Shahram Khazaei, and Azin Movahed (Sharif University of Technology, Tehran).On December 5 to 7, 2022, a general strike took place to put pressure on the regime.

Slogans
Demonstrators used slogans and banners that directly criticized the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran and Khamenei. Protesters showed strong opposition to human rights violations perpetrated by Iran's Guidance Patrol. Protests can take many different forms, from individual statements to mass demonstrations. Protesters may organize a protest as a way of publicly making their opinions heard in an attempt to influence public opinion or government policy, or they may undertake direct action in an attempt to enact desired changes themselves. Women, including schoolchildren, have played a key role in the demonstrations. Since shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Iranian women have been legally required to completely cover their hair in public with a hijab. Enforcement of the unpopular law was eased during the 2013–2021 tenure of President Rouhani, but was then intensified under Rouhani's successor, the hard-line President Ebrahim Raisi.  Bloody Aban  (Persian: آبان خونین), a month near November in the Iranian calendar, was a series of 2019 protests initially caused by a 50–200% increase in fuel prices, and as part of the wider Iranian Democracy Movement, leading to calls for the overthrow of the government in Iran and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

{"final_story": "## The Scarred Valley: A Story of Manipur's Ethnic Tensions

**Characters:**

*   **Anya (16):** A bright, curious student from the Imphal Valley, of Meitei background.
*   **Ren (17):** A thoughtful student from the surrounding hills, of Kuki background.
*   **Mr. Sharma:** Their history and social studies teacher, wise and objective.
*   **Grandpa Thapa:** Ren's grandfather, a repository of Kuki history and traditions.
*   **Auntie Leima:** Anya's aunt, a small business owner in the valley.

**Setting:**

A high school classroom in Manipur, and later, homes in the valley and the hills.

---

The hum of the fluorescent lights in Mr. Sharma's classroom felt particularly heavy that afternoon. A map of Manipur, vibrant in greens and blues, hung prominently, but its beauty was overshadowed by the recent fear and sadness that had gripped the state.

"Good afternoon, class," Mr. Sharma began, his voice softer than usual. "Today, we're going to talk about something difficult, something that has touched all our lives directly or indirectly: the ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur in May 2023. It’s crucial we understand its roots and consequences, not just memorize facts, but to foster empathy and a desire for peace."

Anya, who usually sat eagerly taking notes, felt a knot in her stomach. She’d heard snippets from her parents and seen the news, but the full picture felt too vast and confusing. Ren, usually jovial, sat with a somber expression, his gaze fixed on the map’s hilly regions.

"Let's start with the question: What caused this violence?" Mr. Sharma tapped a pointer on the map. "Manipur is a state of incredible diversity. We have the **Imphal Valley**, home primarily to the **Meitei people**, which is where most of the development and political power are concentrated. Then, we have the **surrounding hills**, vast and beautiful, inhabited by various tribal communities, predominantly the **Kuki** and **Naga peoples**."

He continued, "Historically, there have been differences in laws and regulations between these regions. For instance, **Meiteis, despite forming the majority, are legally restricted from buying land in the tribal hill areas** without special permission. This law was intended to protect the tribal communities' land and traditions. However, the **tribal communities are not restricted from settling in the valley.**"

Anya raised her hand. "Sir, I heard my Auntie Leima say that Meiteis also feel a kind of pressure. She says the valley is getting very crowded, and many Meiteis feel we’re losing space."

Mr. Sharma nodded. "That's a valid point, Anya. Population growth and urbanisation are real pressures. And this brings us to one of the major catalysts: the **demand from some within the Meitei community to be included in the Scheduled Tribes (ST) list.**"

Ren’s hand shot up. "Sar, that's what caused so much fear in the hills!" he blurted out, a tremor in his voice. "If Meiteis get ST status, they can buy land in our areas. We already feel our land is being taken, and this would make it even worse."

Mr. Sharma acknowledged him. "Indeed, Ren. On April 14th, 2023, the High Court ordered the state government to *consider* recommending ST status for the Meitei community. This decision, though a recommendation, was perceived by many tribal communities, especially the Kukis, as a direct threat to their land rights and cultural identity. They feared it would lead to Meitei people acquiring their ancestral lands in the hills, lands that are already scarce and vital for their livelihoods."

"But why was land such a big issue?" Anya asked.

Mr. Sharma explained, "Well, several other factors were already creating immense tension. The state government had begun **evicting Kuki communities from forest reserves**, claiming they were encroaching on government land and to curb poppy cultivation. Many Kuki people felt these evictions were unjust and targeted, labelling them 'anti-tribal.' Also, there's been an **influx of refugees from Myanmar** following the 2021 military coup. While this is a humanitarian issue, some in the Meitei community voiced concerns about population changes and resource strain, associating certain tribal groups with these refugees."

"My Grandpa Thapa told me about the poppy cultivation," Ren added, his voice regaining some strength. "He said that while some people might be involved, it's not fair to evict entire villages and make it seem like all Kuki people are involved in illegal activities. He says we just want to live peacefully on our land."

"Exactly," Mr. Sharma affirmed. "These actions, coupled with the High Court ruling, created a powder keg. On **May 3rd, 2023, the All Tribal Students' Union Manipur (ATSUM) organized a 'Tribal Solidarity March' in all hill districts** to protest the ST status recommendation and the perceived anti-tribal policies. Tragically, in one of these rallies, in a region bordering Bishnupur district, demonstrators clashed with another group. This sparked the initial fires of violence."

---

The classroom discussion continued for days as Mr. Sharma carefully laid out the complex tapestry of historical grievances, legal interpretations, and political actions. He spoke of the **perception of political power being concentrated in the valley** (39 out of 60 legislative assembly seats won by Meitei candidates in the last election), leading to frustration among tribal groups who felt their regions were neglected in terms of development. He also mentioned incidents like the **demolition of churches in the Tribal Colony of Imphal**, which further inflamed religious tensions, as many Kuki people are Christian and Meiteis are largely Hindu.

"It seems like a lot of historical problems and current actions just came together at once," Anya said one day, trying to process it all.

"Precisely," Mr. Sharma agreed. "It wasn't a single cause, but a confluence of factors. And unfortunately, the consequences have been devastating."

---

**The Consequences:**

The class transitioned to the somber reality of the violence's impact. Mr. Sharma projected statistics on the board.

"As of early July, **over 140 people have been killed, more than 300 wounded, and approximately 54,000 people displaced.**"

Anya gasped. "Fifty-four thousand? That's like an entire small town disappearing!"

"It is," Mr. Sharma said gravely. "Think about what that means: homes burnt, livelihoods destroyed, communities shattered. People who lived side-by-side for generations now view each other with fear and suspicion."

Ren's voice was hoarse. "My uncle's house in Imphal was burnt. They had to flee to a relief camp. My youngest cousin, she's only five, she keeps asking if they can go home. But there's nothing left."

Anya felt a pang of guilt. Her Auntie Leima’s business had been affected by the shutdowns, but her home was safe. "My aunt also mentioned some Meitei families had to leave their homes in the hills too, seeking refuge. It sounds like everyone suffered."

"That's a crucial point, Anya," Mr. Sharma emphasized. "While the violence escalated from specific events, *both* communities have suffered immense losses. Homes of Kuki families in the valley were targeted, and Meitei families in the hills also had to flee. The violence doesn't discriminate once it takes hold."

He then spoke about the deeper consequences:

*   **Loss of Trust and Deepened Divides:** "The fabric of social harmony has been severely damaged. Trust between communities, which takes generations to build, is easily shattered. People are now identifying more strongly with their ethnic groups, sometimes at the expense of seeing themselves as fellow Manipuris or even fellow human beings."
*   **Humanitarian Crisis:** "The displaced individuals are living in relief camps, facing uncertainty about their future. Children are out of school, families are separated, and the trauma of witnessing violence will linger for years."
*   **Economic Setbacks:** "Businesses have been destroyed, trade routes disrupted, and the overall economy of Manipur has suffered greatly. Rebuilding will be a long and arduous process."
*   **Weaponization of Identity:** "As the conflict unfolded," Mr. Sharma explained, "we saw how identities – Meitei, Kuki, Hindu, Christian – were used by some to fuel hatred and justify violence. This is common in many conflicts; it’s easier to fight an 'other' than to address complex underlying issues."
*   **Allegations of Bias and Impunity:** "Concerns have been raised about the impartiality of some security forces and political statements that seemed to favor one group over another. This erodes public confidence in institutions meant to protect all citizens equally."

He concluded, "The government has initiated steps to address this. A **panel led by a retired Chief Justice** will investigate the violence, and the **CBI will probe specific cases** to ensure a neutral investigation. A peace committee is also being established. But true healing will require much more than investigations and committees. It requires dialogue, understanding, and a willingness from all sides to prioritize peace."

Ren looked at Anya, and Anya looked back, a shared sadness in their eyes. They had both heard the stories, felt the impact, and now, they understood the complex, tragic narrative.

"What can we do, Sir?" Anya asked, her voice small.

Mr. Sharma offered a hopeful smile. "You, my students, can do the most important thing: learn, empathize, and refuse to let hatred take root. Engage in respectful dialogue. Challenge misinformation. Advocate for peace. Because the future of Manipur, and indeed any community scarred by conflict, depends on the next generation choosing unity over division."

The bell rang, but the lesson lingered, a heavy reminder of the fragility of peace and the imperative to build it stronger, together. Manipur is a hill state in northeast India, bordering Myanmar to its east and south. The central area is the Imphal Valley occupying about 10% of the land area of the state, which is mainly populated by the Meitei people. The surrounding hills which are undeveloped are inhabited by hill tribes, who are classified as Kukis in the southern portion and Nagas in the northeastern portion.The Meiteis, who are largely Hindus, make up 53% of the population. Samir looked down at his desk. "So, it wasn't just about business practices, but about the company culture itself."

Rio mengangguk. "Oh, aku tahu itu! Aku pernah melihatnya di film-film. Jadi, tujuannya untuk mengenang orang-orang terkenal atau peristiwa penting, kan?"

"Tepat sekali!" Maya melanjutkan. "Plakat Biru ini seperti penanda sejarah resmi. Mereka merayakan para ilmuwan, seniman, politikus, dan tokoh-tokoh hebat lainnya yang pernah tinggal atau bekerja di suatu tempat. "Sekarang, mari kita beralih ke Plakat Pelangi," kata Maya, mengganti tampilan di laptopnya. Kali ini, gambar yang muncul adalah plakat biru melingkar dengan enam warna pelangi di sekelilingnya. "Betul!" Maya mengiyakan. "Bayangkan kita berada di York, di depan sebuah rumah tua. **Perbandingan dan Keunikan**

"Jadi, apa perbandingan utamanya?" Rio bertanya, mulai membuat daftar di catatannya.

Maya menjelaskan, "Keduanya adalah program plakat peringatan di Inggris. Keduanya ingin melestarikan sejarah dan mengenang figur penting. Tapi ada beberapa perbedaan kunci:

*   **Fokus Sejarah:** Plakat Biru lebih umum, mencakup berbagai bidang dan tokoh. Plakat Pelangi secara spesifik berfokus pada sejarah dan warisan LGBTQIA+. Ini adalah upaya untuk mengisi kesenjangan dalam representasi sejarah.

"Kau tahu, ada juga yang namanya Plakat Pink," tambah Maya. "Ini sedikit berbeda. Sebelum Plakat Pelangi muncul, ide Plakat Pink sudah ada. Awalnya, Plakat Pink sering digunakan untuk mengenang korban Holocaust yang gay atau korban kekerasan anti-gay. Jadi, ada nuansa peringatan tragedi yang lebih kuat."

"Oh, jadi lebih ke arah memorial?" tanya Rio.

"Ya, pada awalnya," jawab Maya. "Tapi di Inggris, ide Plakat Pink juga berkembang untuk merayakan warisan LGBT secara lebih luas. Ada buku panduan Plakat Pink di London pada tahun 1986, dan bahkan ada aplikasi ponsel untuk menemukan Plakat Pink di Brighton. Jadi, meskipun warnanya sama-sama 'non-biru', tujuannya bisa sedikit berbeda, atau setidaknya memiliki sejarah yang berbeda dalam penggunaannya."

**Mengapa Ini Penting?**

Maya menutup laptopnya dan menatap Rio. "Bayangkan jika kita tidak punya Plakat Pelangi, Rio. Banyak kisah penting, seperti kisah Anne Lister, atau Black Lesbian and Gay Centre yang menjadi tempat aman bagi banyak orang kulit hitam LGBTQIA+, atau London Lighthouse yang membantu penderita HIV/AIDS ketika stigma masih sangat tinggi, mungkin akan dilupakan. "Aku rasa ini adalah cara yang indah untuk menceritakan kembali sejarah," katanya, matanya berbinar. Emulating established UK blue plaque programmes run by English Heritage, local authorities and other bodies, the first permanent rainbow plaque (a blue circular plaque with six rainbow colours around the circumference) was unveiled in York in July 2018. Some UK LGBT locations are denoted by pink plaques, an idea that predated rainbow plaques.

History
The rainbow plaque programme was initiated in 2018 by York Civic Trust and the York LGBT Forum to honour lesbian diarist Anne Lister (1791–1840) and her partner Ann Walker, with the first version of a plaque unveiled on 24 July 2018, replaced with amended wording including the word 'lesbian' in February 2019. Temporary cardboard plaques were also placed on key sites during LGBT pride campaigns in York in 2018 and Leeds in 2019.The permanent plaque initiative then extended nationally through the Wandsworth LGBTQ+ Forum and Studio Voltaire, unveiling permanent plaques for Oscar Wilde at Clapham Junction railway station on 24 July 2019, and for the 1980s film My Beautiful Laundrette on Wilcox Road in South Lambeth on 10 September 2021.In 2023, five further rainbow plaques were announced for London, supported by the Mayor of London's Untold Stories Fund and Wandsworth Oasis.

The air was crisp, the scent of impending winter hung heavy, and the festive season was just around the corner in Sheffield, December 2022. But for thousands of residents in the northwestern suburbs, particularly Hillsborough, Malin Bridge, and Stannington, the usual warmth of their homes was about to be replaced by a chilling silence. This is the story of the "Silent Flood," a major gas supply outage that plunged parts of Sheffield into a cold, dark two weeks.

### Chapter 1: The Unseen Enemy Beneath

Our story begins on the evening of **December 2nd, 2022**. Picture Bankfield Lane in Stannington, a quiet street like many others. Deep beneath the surface, an old **asbestos-cement mainline pipe**, installed all the way back in 1970, was silently battling an internal struggle. This pipe, part of the **Yorkshire Water network**, was designed to carry clean drinking water to homes.

Suddenly, with a groan that no one above ground could hear, the pipe gave way. It **burst**. This wasn't a small leak; it was a catastrophic failure. More than **2 million litres of water** – that’s enough to fill three Olympic-sized swimming pools – began to gush out.

Now, here's where the problem became truly unique and devastating. This gushing water didn't just flood the street. It found its way into the **Cadent Gas network**, the intricate web of underground pipes that carries natural gas to homes for heating and cooking. Imagine a giant, hidden underground river, now flowing not with gas, but with water.

### Chapter 2: Water in the Wires (and Pipes!)

As the water surged through the gas mains, it began to flow downhill, following the natural contours of the land through Stannington and Hillsborough. The consequences were immediate and alarming.

Around **midnight**, emergency services were called. They went door-to-door, waking residents, not because of a fire, but because water was starting to overflow. Inside homes, water was bubbling out of gas meters and even from gas stoves! Outdoors, manhole covers were lifting, and water was seeping from the bases of streetlights. It was a surreal and unprecedented situation. **Cadent Gas**, the company responsible for the gas network, described it as something they had "never had to deal with before."

By **December 3rd**, the scale of the disaster was becoming clear. More than **1,000 properties** were without a gas supply. To make matters worse, many homes in the immediate vicinity of the burst water main also experienced reduced or no water supply for several days.

Cadent Gas engineers faced a monumental task. They couldn't just turn the gas back on; the pipes were full of water! First, they had to go to each affected property individually and **turn off the gas supply at the meter** to prevent further damage and ensure safety. This was a painstaking process. More than **100 engineers** were drafted in, working 24 hours a day, a number that soon swelled to over 200.

### Chapter 3: The Deep Freeze and the Major Incident

As the days passed, the situation worsened. By **December 6th**, the number of properties without gas had risen to **over 2,000**, extending further down the hillsides into Hillsborough. The initial heavy rainfall that accompanied the burst main turned into bitterly cold temperatures and even snowfall. Temperatures plummeted, reaching as low as **-3°C (27°F)** on December 9th.

With no central heating, residents were struggling. They relied on electric heaters, which put a massive strain on the local electricity network. **Northern Powergrid**, the electricity supplier, had to advise residents to use heaters sparingly to avoid complete power outages. Despite these warnings, some streets in Stannington began to experience intermittent power cuts.

The severity of the situation led the **Sheffield City Council** to declare a **major incident on December 7th**. This declaration was crucial because it allowed local authorities to better coordinate the massive response needed. At this point, only about a quarter of the affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected. Cadent Gas engineers, despite their tireless efforts, were battling to pump vast quantities of water out of a complex and extensive underground network. Equipment and engineers were brought in from across the country to assist.

### Chapter 4: The Long Road to Recovery

The outage was a test of resilience for the community. Local businesses and authorities stepped up. Refuge spaces were opened, offering warmth, hot food, and drinks. Lomas Hall became a central hub, providing portable electric heaters and hotplates. The Peacock Inn and Crown & Glove pubs offered food, drinks, and even showering facilities. Schools remained open, using electric heaters and advising students to dress warmly.

By **December 10th**, Cadent Gas reported that around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected. However, significant challenges remained in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes were still without gas. The process of draining water from such a vast and intricate network was incredibly difficult.

The outage, which started on **December 2nd**, dragged on for almost two weeks for some properties. While many were reconnected sooner, some residents endured the cold and inconvenience until around **December 16th**, marking a nearly **two-week period without gas**.

### Chapter 5: Lessons Learned and Lasting Impact

The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

The local population uses the large spaces of the Kyzylkum Desert as a pasture for livestock (mostly sheep, Bactrian camels and dromedaries).
The desert is well known for its deposits of gold, uranium, copper, aluminium and silver, natural gas and oil. The development of the most famous gold-field at Muruntau began in the early 1970s. The centres for the mining and smelting industry at the region are Navoi, Zarafshan, Uchkuduk. The major industrial enterprises are: НГМК (Navoi Mining and Smelting Complex) and the Uzbek U.S.A. Joint Venture "Zarafshan-Newmont". The centres of the gas-production industry are Gazli and Mubarek.

***

**Yeti Airlines Penerbangan 691: Sebuah Pelajaran dari Langit Pokhara**

Langit di atas Pokhara, Nepal, pada 15 Januari 2023, seharusnya menjadi kanvas biru yang damai. Namun, bagi 72 orang di dalam pesawat Yeti Airlines Penerbangan 691, hari itu berubah menjadi tragedi yang tak terlupakan. Kecelakaan ini bukan hanya merenggut nyawa, tetapi juga membuka mata kita terhadap kompleksitas dan pentingnya setiap detail dalam penerbangan.

Pesawat ATR 72 itu, dengan nomor penerbangan 691, sedang dalam perjalanan domestik dari Kathmandu menuju Pokhara. Ini adalah penerbangan rutin, seperti ratusan penerbangan lainnya setiap hari. Namun, saat mendekati Bandara Internasional Pokhara yang baru dibuka, sesuatu yang mengerikan terjadi.

**Detik-detik Menuju Tragedi**

Rekaman video dari darat menunjukkan pesawat itu berbelok tajam ke kiri, sayapnya miring drastis, sebelum akhirnya menabrak tepi Sungai Seti Gandaki. Sebuah video lain, yang disiarkan langsung oleh seorang penumpang di Facebook, menunjukkan betapa tak siapnya para penumpang menghadapi musibah itu. Pukul 10:56:27, saat pesawat berada di ketinggian sekitar 721 kaki di atas permukaan tanah, Pilot yang Terbang (PF) menonaktifkan sistem Autopilot. Ini adalah bagian dari prosedur pendaratan.

Namun, di sinilah letak masalahnya. Data FDR menunjukkan bahwa pada saat itu, tidak ada pergerakan flap. Sebaliknya, kecepatan putaran baling-baling (propeller) kedua mesin menurun drastis hingga kurang dari 25%, dan torsi (tenaga) mesin turun menjadi 0%. Ini adalah indikasi bahwa baling-baling telah masuk ke kondisi "feathered".

**Apa itu "Feathered Condition"?**

Bayangkan baling-baling pesawat seperti kipas angin. Dalam kondisi normal, bilah-bilah kipas angin itu miring untuk mendorong udara dan menghasilkan dorongan. Dalam kondisi "feathered", bilah-bilah itu diputar hingga sejajar dengan arah aliran udara. Tujuannya adalah untuk mengurangi hambatan aerodinamis jika mesin mati di udara, sehingga pesawat bisa meluncur lebih jauh. Namun, dalam kondisi ini, mesin tidak akan menghasilkan dorongan sama sekali!

Tim investigasi menemukan bahwa baling-baling pesawat telah "feathered" selama satu menit sebelum kecelakaan. Ini berarti pesawat terbang tanpa dorongan mesin selama satu menit! Yang lebih mengejutkan, tuas pengontrol baling-baling (condition levers), ditemukan dalam posisi "feathered" di reruntuhan.

Para ahli berspekulasi bahwa karena tuas "condition levers" dan tuas flap berada berdekatan di kokpit ATR 72, PM, Kamal KC, mungkin secara tidak sengaja menggerakkan tuas "condition levers" alih-alih tuas flap saat diminta oleh PF. Meskipun sekitar dua puluh detik kemudian dia menggerakkan tuas flap dengan benar, dia gagal menyadari kesalahan sebelumnya. Ini menunjukkan bahwa daftar periksa pendaratan (landing checklist) tidak diikuti dengan benar.

Ketika ATC memberikan izin mendarat pada 10:57:07, PF menyebutkan dua kali bahwa tidak ada tenaga dari mesin. Mereka bahkan menggerakkan tuas tenaga ke posisi maksimum, tetapi sudah terlambat. Pesawat telah kehilangan dorongan dan kecepatan, menyebabkan "stall" – kondisi di mana sayap tidak lagi dapat menghasilkan gaya angkat yang cukup untuk menopang pesawat.

Kecelakaan Yeti Airlines Penerbangan 691 adalah pengingat yang menyakitkan akan pentingnya:

1.  **Kepatuhan Terhadap Prosedur:** Setiap prosedur, setiap daftar periksa, dirancang untuk keselamatan. Penyimpangan sekecil apa pun dapat berakibat fatal.
2.  **Komunikasi dan Verifikasi:** Meskipun komunikasi terjadi di kokpit, verifikasi ulang sangat penting, terutama untuk tindakan kritis.

On 15 January 2023, the aircraft being operated on the route, an ATR 72 flown by Yeti Airlines, crashed while landing at Pokhara, killing all 72 occupants on board. It is the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.

Accident
The flight took off from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport at 10:33 am NST. It crashed on the bank of the Seti Gandaki River while on final approach to landing at Pokhara International Airport. A video filmed from the ground showed the aircraft banking steeply to the left before crashing 65 metres (213 ft) away. Another video was streamed live on Facebook by Sonu Jaiswal, a passenger on the plane, before and during the crash. The aircraft involved in the crash was a 15-year-old twin-engine turboprop ATR 72-500, with serial number 754 and registration 9N-ANC. It was first delivered to Kingfisher Airlines as VT-KAJ in 2007. The airport was closed as authorities launched a rescue operation. The Government of Nepal summoned an emergency cabinet meeting following the crash. The Office of the Prime Minister declared 16 January to be a national day of mourning, and the flag of Nepal was flown at half-staff. Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: How many teams participate in the Turkish Women's Football Super League, and what is the format of the league?

target_age: "15-18"
story_style: "educational"
language: "Indonesian"

Context:
The Turkish Women's Football Super League (Turkish: Kadınlar Süper Ligi), formerly the First Women's Football League (also known as the Turkcell Women's Football Super League for sponsorship reasons), is the top level women's football league of Turkey. In the 2022–23 season, one group of 10 teams and one group of nine teams play a double round robin and finals to decide a champion club, which qualifies for a spot in the UEFA Women's Champions League.On 8 March 2021, the International Women's Day, the Turkish Football Federation signed a sponsorship agreement with the Turkish mobile phone operator Turkcell. Accordingly, the First Women's Football League was named Turkcell Women's Super League (Turkish: Turkcell Kadın Süper Ligi) beginning with the 2021–22 season.

Format
In an effort to increase quality of the league, in the 2009–10 season two teams were relegated and four teams were promoted to the first league. Thus, the 2010–11 season consisted of twelve teams. Fashion One TV became the official media sponsor of the league for the 2010–11 season. At this time the league gained little attention in Turkey. After playing two groups with six teams and then having a championship and relegation group, the 2012–13 season was played as a double-round robin with ten teams again. The winner after 18 games was the champion and qualifies for the UEFA Women's Champions League, the bottom two teams get relegated. In 2016–17 there again was introduced a championship and relegation round after the regular season.
For the 2019-20 league season, the number of participating teams was increased from ten to twelve again after eight seasons. No relegation was planned to take place, so that the planned number of teams would be achieved with two promoted teams from the Women's Second League. However, Trabzon İdmanocağı had to be relegated since they did not show up in the entire previous season. To replace them, a third team from the Second League was promoted. All three women's leagues of the 2019-20 season were stopped on 8 March 2020 due to COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey.Due to the ongoing pandemic, the 2020-21 season of the Women's First Football League, after renaming the Turkcell Women's Football League, will take start with delay on 17 April 2021. The season was dedicated to healthcare workers, and named 2021 Turkish Turkcell Women's Football League Healthcare Workers' Season (Turkish: 2021 Sağlık Çalışanları Futbol Ligi). The league consisted of 16 teams, including all the 12 teams from the previous season and 4 teams promoted from the Second League's previous season. The teams were divided into four groups of four teams each, with one promoted team in each group. Each team in the group played only three matches in a round-robin tournament. The top two teams of the four groups play quarter-finals and semi-finals in Single-elimination tournament. The winner of the final match, on 4 May 2021, represented Turkey at the 2021–22 UEFA Women's Champions League.

"Alright class, settle down, settle down!" Mr. Ivanov, a history teacher with a passion for architectural evolution, tapped his pen against the interactive whiteboard. "Today, we're not just looking at dates, but at growth, adaptation, and how a city's needs shape its structures. Our subject? The Inter Expo Center in Sofia, Bulgaria."

"Precisely, Maya," Mr. Ivanov smiled. "Many of you have probably walked past it, maybe even attended an event there. But how many of you know its story?" He projected an image of the sleek, modern façade of the Inter Expo Center (IEC). "Imagine, if you will, the year **2001**." He gestured to the screen, where a slightly older, less expansive image of the IEC appeared. "This is when the Inter Expo Center, a vibrant new venue, first burst onto the scene in Sofia. "Just two halls?" exclaimed David, surprised. "It has six now!"

"Wow, so the congress halls are actually older than some of the exhibition halls?" wondered Lena, taking notes diligently.

"That's a very keen observation, Lena! Yes, the congress facilities were a crucial early addition," Mr. Ivanov commended. "But the growth didn't stop there. As Sofia's reputation as a business and cultural hub grew, so did the need for even more exhibition space. Therefore, in **2008**, the center expanded once more, opening **further exhibition halls** to accommodate even larger international events. By this point, the IEC was well on its way to becoming the biggest convention and exhibition venue in the city."

He paused, a knowing smile playing on his lips. "Now, picture this: you’ve just attended an incredible expo, your mind buzzing with new ideas and connections. You step outside, and you need to get home. What's the most convenient way?"

Mr. Ivanov brought up a final image, showing a panoramic view of the bustling Inter Expo Center today, with its six exhibition halls, eight congress halls, and surrounding amenities.

"So, to recap," he concluded, "the Inter Expo Center in Sofia didn't just 'appear' overnight. It began its journey in **2001** with two initial exhibition halls. It grew in **2003** with the addition of its congress center and another exhibition hall. Further exhibition halls were added in **2008**, solidifying its position as a major player. And its integration into Sofia's urban fabric was cemented in **2012** with its very own Metro station. Finally, a significant internal upgrade in **2019** ensures its facilities remain top-tier. It's a continuous story of adaptation, expansion, and a testament to Sofia's dynamic growth."

"From two halls to six, with a huge congress center and its own Metro station," Maya mused. "It's like watching a small seed grow into a huge, thriving tree."

"An excellent analogy, Maya," Mr. Ivanov beamed. "And just like a thriving tree, the Inter Expo Center continues to be a vital landmark, hosting countless events that shape Sofia's economic and cultural landscape." He gestured to the board.
